We answer this with a post-hoc audit of a published TikTok classifier, holding all three stages to one significance standard using only its logged decisions, labels, and pre-fusion features, with source language as the subgroup axis. The asymmetry is significant at the stage deciding what the model may read, and again in what the text branch encodes. At the earlier stage, a language-blind cap admits less of a Vietnamese clip than an English one, for reasons of segmentation, not verbosity. The asymmetry is undetectable at the decision, where the smallest subgroup leaves twelve items to test. An audit reading only decisions looks where its evidence is thinnest; the same test staged upstream recovers a disparity the decision-level view returns as noise.

papers.title: An Exact Branch-Price-and-Cut Algorithm for the Vehicle Routing Problem with Floating Targets
papers.abstract: The Vehicle Routing Problem with Floating Targets (VRPFT) is a generalization of the capacitated vehicle routing problem where targets may actively move to locations ''convenient'' for the vehicles. In particular, each target may leave its home location at a bounded speed. A solution to the VRPFT is a sequence of targets for each vehicle to visit and a meeting point in space-time for each target. In this paper, we solve the VRPFT exactly with a branch-price-and-cut algorithm. Our key contribution is a dominance criterion for the pricing labeling algorithm that utilizes closed-form lower and upper bounds on a vehicle's trajectory cost given a fixed sequence of targets. We prove that the criterion preserves optimality, and the algorithm has smaller computation time than the exact dynamic program of prior work on identical hardware. We also provide a relaxed criterion that prunes more aggressively; the resulting heuristic is faster than our exact algorithm and matched every certified optimum on the benchmark.

papers.title: Who Is Ego? Scaling Cross-View Camera Wearer Identification and Segmentation beyond Humans
papers.abstract: A first-person (ego) image reveals what a camera sees, but not who or what carries it. Given a synchronized third-person (exo) image, camera wearer identification asks who is ego: which candidate carries the ego camera? We extend this task beyond humans to robots, vehicles, animals, and drones, and broaden its spatial scope (where is ego) from selecting a provided candidate mask to wearer segmentation with absence prediction and mutual camera localization across ego-exo views. We introduce FindEgo-1M, comprising 1.16M real and simulated ego-exo pairs across 12 wearer types, 17 domains, and 111 test settings. Our approach exploits a geometric relation: the ego camera's projection into the exo image, i.e., the epipole, lies on or near its wearer. We introduce EgoRay-ZS, the first method to turn a frozen feed-forward 3D reconstruction model, VGGT-$Ω$, into a training-free solution for wearer identification and segmentation. Its geometric readout ranks candidate masks or segmentation proposals by angular offset and distance to the ego camera, while the relative pose provides mutual camera directions. We then develop the full EgoRay model through pose-supervised training on FindEgo-1M and label-free test-time adaptation constrained by candidate masks. Without task-specific training, EgoRay-ZS achieves 78.0% identification accuracy on TF2023's original labels, versus 52.9% reported for the dataset-trained PEN. On FindEgo-1M, EgoRay achieves state-of-the-art chance-corrected accuracy of 87.1 and 77.7 on seen and unseen settings. On matched queries, EgoRay also outperforms GPT-6 Astra by 31.6 and 21.3 points on seen and unseen settings, respectively, while running $18\times$ faster. Data, code, and models will be released.

papers.title: Computing Feasible EF1 Allocations under Generalized Assignment Constraints
papers.abstract: We study the fair allocation of indivisible goods under generalized assignment constraints, where each agent's bundle must fit within her budget, the sizes of goods may differ across agents, and unallocated goods go to a charity. A natural fairness notion here is feasible envy-freeness up to one good (FEF1), which requires an agent's envy towards any feasible subset of another bundle to disappear after some good is removed from this subset. While FEF1 allocations always exist, they could previously be computed efficiently only when sizes are common to all agents. We show that FEF1 allocations can be computed in strongly polynomial time, and more generally whenever each agent's value can be almost exactly maximized over her feasible bundles, a requirement that cannot be relaxed substantially. Our analysis relies on an essentially tight quadratic bound on how often each agent's bundle is repaired. Moreover, the allocation can be made approximately envy-free up to any good while retaining nearly half the Nash welfare of any given allocation. In contrast, requiring a single good to eliminate an agent's envy towards all feasible subsets of another bundle at once, which makes no difference without constraints, renders the problem NP-hard and may halve the attainable Nash welfare.

papers.title: Superconformal Index Identities for Dual Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We study superconformal index identities for three classes of dual four-dimensional gauge theories. For $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory with gauge groups $SO(2n+1)$ and $USp(2n)$, we prove at every rank the equality of flavored Schur indices predicted by $S$-duality, using Rains's diagonal trace transformation. For Kutasov--Schwimmer duality with adjoint superpotential $\textrm{Tr} X^{k+1}$, we prove the index identity between $SU(k+1)$ and $SU(k-1)$ with two flavors at independent elliptic nomes $p,q$, in the ultraviolet assignment $R(Q)=0$. On the locus $p=q^k$, we reduce the identity to that of ordinary supersymmetric QCD whenever the specialized expressions are generically regular. Finally, we test the dualities conjectured by Cho and Song between quiver and single-group descriptions of four families of Argyres--Douglas theories. For the rank-one $H_1$ theory we prove equality of the two full flavored indices, and for each family at arbitrary rank we evaluate the generalized Coulomb index in both descriptions, obtaining the product formula conjectured by Buican and Jiang.

papers.title: Resource theory of pi-ordered imaginarity and its resource quantifiers
papers.abstract: Conventional resource theory of quantum imaginarity takes real density matrices as free states without ordering constraints on their diagonal populations. Motivated by the role of population ordering in the incoherent ergotropy of quantum batteries and the recently proposed framework of $π$-ordered coherence, we develop the resource theory of $π$-ordered imaginarity. In this refined framework, free states are required to be real in the reference basis and to obey a prescribed permutation order $π$ for their diagonal populations. This theory thereby identifies two independent quantum resources: complex phases and population misordering, where the latter is inaccessible within the standard imaginarity resource theory. We characterize the structure of free states using majorization and the Schur-Horn theorem, define admissible $π$-ordered real operations, and examine their intersection with $π$-ordered incoherent operations. We further construct resource quantifiers for the $π$-ordered imaginarity based on relative entropy, fidelity and robustness, and derive inequalities relating the robustness of $π$-ordered imaginarity and that of $π$-ordered coherence. The present framework generalizes the standard resource theory of imaginarity to incorporate population ordering and is naturally suited for thermodynamic settings such as quantum batteries.

papers.title: SkySearcher: High-Altitude Onboard VLM Reasoning for Aerial Semantic Search
papers.abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have improved semantic and visual reasoning, enabling UAVs to search for open-vocabulary queries in unstructured environments at high altitude. However, existing systems mainly follow low-altitude strategies, focusing on close-range iterative exploration, requiring storage-intensive dense 3D metric-semantic reconstructions or relying on large cloud-serviced VLMs assuming constant internet access. We propose SkySearcher, an aerial semantic search navigation method designed for large outdoor scenes. SkySearcher integrates onboard VLM reasoning with a lightweight probabilistic representation that guides an information-driven exploration. The VLM extracts semantic information at high altitude about the target or cues informing about its location. This information is projected to the ground using the camera frustum instead of limited-depth sensors, actively exploiting the expansive field of view offered by elevated sensing. The information regarding the presence or absence of semantic cues is then integrated into a probabilistic map by modeling the spatial belief of the query, maintaining a task-driven memory for the mission and guiding the exploration towards semantically promising regions. Extensive simulations for Aerial Object Goal Navigation on public benchmarks demonstrate that SkySearcher significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in success rate, flight time, and navigation precision, while a deployment of SkySercher running fully onboard a drone demonstrates the applicability of our approach.

papers.title: Mode-resolved spin-wave spectroscopy by a single paramagnetic center
papers.abstract: We demonstrate mode-resolved ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) spectroscopy using optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) of a single nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in (111)-oriented diamond. A two-tone drive couples the magnetization dynamics to the NV spin resonance via the magnon Kerr effect. We show that the NV can detect the static stray field produced by this effect down to precession cone angles $θ\approx \SI{1}{\degree}$, providing a generic scheme to measure the linear FMR spectrum with the spatial resolution of an atomic-size probe. We validate the approach on a normally magnetized yttrium iron garnet (YIG) microdisk, resolving its intrinsic quantized spin-wave modes. Scanning the probe across the surface, we map the spatial profile of the modes and find quantitative agreement with analytical models.

papers.title: Fast Fluid Antenna Multiple Access: Exact Analysis and Fixed-Aperture Asymptotics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the interference-limited outage performance of fast fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA), in which the receive port is selected according to the instantaneous symbol-based signal-to-interference energy ratio. For any positive-definite spatial covariance matrix and an arbitrary finite number of candidate ports, we show that constant-modulus multiuser interference admits an exact reduction to the comparison of two independent correlated exponential random vectors. This representation leads to a nonnegative double multi-index series for the outage probability, a recursive coefficient evaluation, and a certified truncation-error bound. We then study the distinct asymptotic regime where the number of candidate ports goes to infinity while the physical aperture remains unchanged, assuming exponential spatial correlation. For this model, we derive an explicit finite-port series requiring no numerical integration, and characterize continuous port selection through a convergent one-dimensional series for arbitrary thresholds. The analysis further yields an exact expression relating the maximum supportable number of users to the antenna aperture size and target outage probability. Numerical results validate the finite-port and asymptotic analyses, and illustrate that given sufficient aperture size, a user utilizing fast FAMA can overcome a massive number of interferers for decent communication performance.

papers.title: Seebeck and Hall effects in charge-neutral ballistic graphene as probes of electron-electron interactions
papers.abstract: Electron-hole asymmetry of the Coulomb velocity renormalization is responsible for finite Seebeck and Hall coefficients in charge-neutral graphene. In the ballistic regime the thermopower is small, $0.1$--$1~μ$V/K, because the chemical-potential shift required by $n_e{=}n_h$ cancels its leading part. When the electron-electron scattering length falls below the sample length, the thermopower crosses over to a collision-dominated value of $4$--$10~μ$V/K, that is an order of magnitude larger. This crossover is a direct thermoelectric marker of the breakdown of ballistic transport and a baseline for identifying the Dirac fluid.

papers.title: High-Throughput GPU Decoding of Quantum Bivariate Bicycle Codes under Circuit-Level Noise
papers.abstract: Bivariate bicycle (BB) codes reduce the physical-qubit overhead of quantum error correction compared to other codes such as Surface codes, but circuit-level faults create dependencies across measurement rounds that limit decoding throughput. We present a parallel-window GPU decoder that combines reusable fault patterns, compact shared-memory state, and persistent GPU workers using min-sum with Relay-BP recovery. On an RTX 5090, the proposed decoder keeps pace with one syndrome round every 1 $μ$s across all four evaluated codes, up to [[144,12,12]] with 63-144 $μ$s median commit delays. This rate has not been demonstrated in prior circuit-level GPU decoding studies and it provides $120\times$ higher decoding throughput than sequential sliding-window decoding. Checking neighboring detector rounds before accepting a decoding result reduces failure rates by up to 65%. For [[144,12,12]] at $p=0.002$, our proposed decoder achieves $7.58\times 10^{-6}$ failures per round, 36% lower than the published belief propagation (BP) with syndrome flipping (BP-SF) result.

papers.title: ProManO: Beyond Sim(3) for Metric Upgrade of Feed-Forward Geometry with Visual-Inertial Anchors
papers.abstract: Upgrading feed-forward geometry to metric scale with visual-inertial odometry (VIO) raises the question of which correction should align dense feed-forward prediction with sparse metric VIO anchors. Existing methods use either a similarity transformation, which cannot represent depth-dependent distortion, or a projective transformation, which alters pre-calibrated intrinsics. We prove that the transformations compatible with pre-calibrated intrinsics form a ten-dimensional manifold. Beyond Sim(3), this manifold contains three degrees of freedom (DoF) that locate the plane at infinity and leave residuals growing quadratically with depth range after any similarity alignment. These DoF are invisible in the image and can be resolved only by metric depth along viewing rays or by multi-view constraints. To estimate them, we propose ProManO, a probabilistic manifold optimization framework in which every anchor is weighted by its along-ray uncertainty and inlier probability within a single expectation-maximization (EM) procedure. ProManO certifies the similarity synchronization and refines the plane at infinity only where it is observable, which guarantees an objective value no worse than that of the optimal similarity alignment. Experiments on EuRoC, CID-SIMS, Oxford Spires, and KITTI-360 demonstrate that ProManO achieves the highest mean F1 and outperforms Sim(3) alignment on all four datasets. The project page is available at https://h0xg.github.io/ProManO/.

papers.title: Backpropagation as Dirac-bracket dynamics of dissipative training
papers.abstract: Gradient-based training of a parametric model is the motion of a damped particle in the potential set by the loss. Using the Bateman-Galley doubling of the degrees of freedom, which gives dissipative systems an action principle, we write gradient flow, the heavy-ball method and Nesterov's accelerated gradient method as Hamiltonian systems. We show that, within this Hamiltonian description, backpropagation is Dirac evolution. The activations of a feed-forward network are treated as coordinates of phase space, and the layer equations as constraints. These constraints are second class for every architecture, and Hamilton's equations with the resulting Dirac bracket reproduce training with the exact gradient of the loss, although the Hamiltonian contains only the cost of the network output. The Dirac bracket of an activation with the momenta of the parameters is its Jacobian, the inverse of the constraint matrix contains both the forward and the reverse modes of automatic differentiation, and the errors propagated by backpropagation are the Lagrange multipliers of the layer constraints: the constraint forces of a kinematic chain under the load of the cost. These results hold in the full doubled phase space, not only in the physical limit. The network's part of the constraint algebra is the same for every optimizer, Nesterov's look-ahead adds one layer of momentum-dependent constraints that couple the two copies of the doubled system, and gradient flow is obtained by constructing the Dirac bracket in stages. We confirm these statements numerically to machine precision and train a network by integrating the Dirac flow of its constraints, with no backward pass in the computation.

papers.title: Feed-Forward Adaptive Gaussian Splatting for Interactive Medical Volume Rendering
papers.abstract: Path-traced rendering shows CT and MR volumes with realistic lighting, but it restarts after every change of view, clipping plane or transfer function (TF), the map from voxel intensity to colour and opacity, which limits the frame rate. Feed-forward Gaussian splatting models such as RenderFM predict the Gaussians directly from the volume instead of fitting them to each scan, and are fast. RenderFM, however, handles only CT, runs its network again after every TF edit, has no clipping operator, and places its Gaussians on a uniform 3-mm grid that blurs organ boundaries and cut faces. We present RenderFM-Next, a feed-forward model that addresses these limits. One network handles both CT and MR. Its Gaussians are predicted once per volume: a new TF needs no pass of this network, and a clipping plane cuts them exactly, using operators from prior work. The model predicts coarse 3-mm Gaussians for the whole volume and refines them to 1.5 mm only where refinement improves the image. A small score head ranks the coarse Gaussians by how much refining them would reduce the rendering error; at render time the user chooses how many are refined, and those next to a clipping plane are always refined, which sharpens cut faces. We build a benchmark of about 2,000 CT and MR scans with path-traced references under clinical presets, TF edits and clipping. Our RenderFM-Next improves over RenderFM retrained on this benchmark by 2.8 dB on CT and 2.4 dB on MR and renders a 1600x1600 view in 4-6 ms. Refinement adds 0.30 / 0.69 dB over the same model trained without it (0.51 / 1.17 dB on cut faces), and refining a learned 10% of the coarse Gaussians matches a random 50% with 2.4x fewer Gaussians. Project page: https://gaozhongpai.github.io/renderfmnext/

papers.title: Exact sequences of regular LF-spaces
papers.abstract: We show that the category of regular LF-spaces has all kernels but, unlike the category of regular LB-spaces, does not have all cokernels. Its topological exact structure, maximal exact structure and maximal deflation-exact structure form a strictly increasing chain of proper subclasses of the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs. To the best of the authors' knowledge, regular LF-spaces in particular provide the first natural example of a category that has all kernels but is not preabelian and whose maximal deflation-exact structure is neither two-sided exact nor equal to the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs.

papers.title: TACC: Target-Aware Carrier Compression for Dense-Context Novel View Synthesis
papers.abstract: Recent feed-forward approaches mark a paradigm shift in novel view synthesis by eliminating the reliance on per-scene optimization, directly inferring 3D representations from input views. However, their reliance on global scene-token context incurs substantial memory and latency overhead, constraining their ability to handle increasingly dense source-view contexts. Compressing source representations offers an intuitive way to limit this token budget. Prior general-purpose compression methods are not tailored for novel view synthesis, as their fixed, target-agnostic nature fails to adapt evidence allocation to individual target views. To overcome this, we introduce TACC, a target-aware compression module tailored for feed-forward latent NVS. Specifically, TACC organizes each source view into a progressive carrier hierarchy. Driven by source-target geometric relevance, it adaptively retrieves tokens to dynamically allocate exact computational quotas. This selective retrieval directly yields a compact, target-conditioned representation. Extensive experiments on the RE10K demonstrate that under dense input settings, TACC achieves $9.23\times$ and $64\times$ higher Effective FPS than Full Context on LagerNVS and LVSM, respectively. Effective FPS excludes one-time source encoding and Carrier construction.

papers.title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
papers.abstract: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.

papers.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
papers.abstract: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues $λ_X,λ_Y,λ_Z$, the advantage is governed by $λ_X^2+λ_Y^2+λ_Z^2$. We prove that no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage when this sum is at most one, reduce the general case to the additivity of a Rényi-2 coherent information, and find coded memories that retain a growing advantage within 1% of this threshold. On a superconducting processor, nine simultaneously operated Bell pairs show an advantage that grows or shrinks exponentially with system size, reversing where a parameter-free model predicts. A three-qubit repetition code turns a shrinking advantage into a growing one with all processor and readout errors included, and under dephasing its memory performs better than Bell sampling in any memory frame on a perfect processor.

papers.title: High-performance metapopulation models for epidemic emergencies: Scalability and performance of implicit and explicit mobility representations on CPUs and GPUs
papers.abstract: Epidemics form a subclass of natural disasters impacting countries or entire continents, where suitable reactions might differ substantially across spatio-temporal dimensions. Spatially resolved models based on ordinary differential equations (ODEs) are an efficient modeling approach for large and distributed populations. Commonly referred to as metapopulation models, they allow a realistic representation of spatial heterogeneities and mobility. Yet, their application in epidemic settings under high time pressure requires efficient, parallelized implementations leveraging modern supercomputers. The different ways to represent mobility in metapopulation models affect both epidemic trajectories and computational costs. In contrast to implicit mobility modeling, where populations are coupled through transition and transmission intensities, explicit Lagrangian mobility tracks traveling subpopulations according to their home and current location. In this paper, we compare metapopulation models with implicit and explicit mobility. A four-patch experiment shows that the trajectories of both formulations remain close, but differences increase with the mobility cycle length. We present CPU- and GPU-based parallelizations and analyze fully connected networks with up to 16,384 patches on 128 CPU cores and NVIDIA A100 and H100 GPUs. Roofline analyses show near-maximum performance for the most time-consuming GPU subroutines and identify data reuse and the cost of mobility events as the main performance drivers. Our results show that mobility assumptions, event frequency, numerical solvers, and available hardware need to be considered together when developing metapopulation models for epidemic emergencies. In a synthesized setting with a disease outbreak in central Europe, we show how a worldwide pandemic with 12,865 patches and four billion state variables can be simulated in 24 seconds using GPUs.

papers.title: DiversePlace: Diversity-Seeking Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Macro Placement
papers.abstract: Macro placement is a critical early-stage decision in physical design because macro locations strongly constrain subsequent implementation stages. The task is difficult because these high-impact discrete decisions must be made before downstream quality can be measured accurately, forcing training to rely on fast but imperfect training-time oracles such as half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL). Existing RL-based placers therefore mostly optimize single HPWL-driven solutions, and their long sequential horizons often require heavy search assistance or offline expert data while leaving little room to preserve multiple competitive layouts. We address this gap by making quality-controlled diversity an explicit objective for macro placement. Instead of relying on a single proxy-optimal solution, we maintain a compact archive of HPWL-competitive yet meaningfully different placements for downstream selection. We realize this idea in DiversePlace, a curriculum proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework that combines a quality-gated diversity reward with an expanding placement horizon, enabling from-scratch RL optimization while keeping exploration inside competitive HPWL regions. On the ISPD2005 benchmarks, DiversePlace consistently improves top-5, top-10, and top-20 archive diversity and achieves lower or virtually identical HPWL on all eight designs with better efficiency. Code: https://github.com/William030422/NIPS2026-DiversePlace.

papers.title: Signatures of multiorbital density waves in the electronic Raman response of bilayer nickelates
authors: Luis G. G. V. Dias da Silva
papers.abstract: Recent Raman scattering experiments on bilayer nickelates have revealed pronounced spectral features in the spin-density-wave state, whose microscopic origin remains controversial, with interpretations ranging from two-magnon excitations to electronic transitions across SDW-induced gaps. Here, we demonstrate that the multiorbital electronic structure of low-pressure bilayer nickelates naturally generates distinct orbital-selective Raman signatures in different symmetry channels. Using a two-orbital bilayer model incorporating the $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals in the orthorhombic structure, we analyze the electronic Raman response of the multiorbital spin-spinless double stripe SDW state and show that the $B_{2g}$ response exhibits a peak at the energy scale $(M_{z^2}+M_{x^2})/2$, associated with SDW gap openings in weakly hybridized bands. In contrast, the dominant peak in the $B_{1g}$ channel emerges at the multiorbital energy scale $(M_{z^2}^2+M_{x^2}^2)^{1/2}$, reflecting the strongly hybridized character of the relevant electronic states. These distinct energy scales provide a unified interpretation of several Raman signatures observed in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and offer a means of disentangling the orbital contributions to the SDW order parameters. Our results highlight that in contrast to the superconducting state, Raman peak positions in the SDW state cannot generally be identified with a single SDW gap and establish symmetry-resolved electronic Raman scattering as a sensitive probe of multiorbital density-wave order.

papers.title: Fuel as Identity: Authenticating Inter-Satellite Laser Links after Total Key Compromise
papers.abstract: Optical inter-satellite links form the backbone of entire constellations in low Earth orbit, yet their security rests on keys alone. When an attacker obtains every key of a satellite, no secret is left to authenticate it again. Existing fixes fail, since ground rekeying encrypts new keys under the leaked ones, and post-compromise protocols assume an authenticated start. As a remedy, the satellite's orbit can take over as the trust anchor. The attacker then needs an impostor satellite that blocks and retransmits the beam, a chord beneath the curved orbit. Hence, the blocking point lies off free fall and costs the impostor continuous thrust. We formalize this position-gated adversary and prove, for satellites on a shared circular orbit, a tight lower bound on the propellant cost in delta-v of a point-mass craft that keeps blocking, however it moves. We present OrbitLock, a history-chained protocol that combines this position gate with ML-KEM. Each link authenticates on its own, and we sketch how combining links forces an impostor onto every link. Once the chain outlasts an impostor's propellant, every key back to the first is authenticated retroactively. A satellite thus needs no crosslink key before launch, so none can leak in the supply chain. The same mechanism heals the link after total key compromise, even without compromise awareness. A passive attacker is shut out at the next round, whereas an active one splits the chains and is exposed once its propellant runs out. The chain can then heal after an operator reset. As a result, every Starlink satellite has a partner on whose link a CubeSat-class impostor runs out of propellant in about two days. This holds against one rigid craft per link running the best attack we know, if each terminal enforces a 1 km exclusion zone, while the protocol only uses under 0.02% of the link.

papers.title: Infinite Hyper-Order of Entire Solutions of a First-Order Differential Equation
papers.abstract: Let $φ$ be a transcendental entire function of finite order. We prove that every entire solution of $$g'=e^φg+1$$ has infinite hyper-order. Then we prove the Brück's conjecture.

papers.title: Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory
papers.abstract: We study the trace-distance error in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by a Haar-random unitary followed by partial trace. In the independent and identically distributed setting, we determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for soft covering with independent codewords, uniform convex splitting, and Haar partial-trace decoupling. For privacy amplification, we determine the exact reliability function for independent random binning and the exact strong converse exponent for every two-universal hash ensemble. The reliability and strong converse formulas involve sandwiched and Petz-Rényi information, respectively. The proofs connect trace-distance errors to quantum hypothesis testing, using Rosenthal inequalities for sums of random matrices in the reliability analysis and conditional second-moment bounds for the strong converses.

papers.title: Attacking Hard-Label Large Vision-Language Models with Model-Sensitive Adversarial Patch Designs
papers.abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in handling multi-modal downstream tasks, gaining increasing popularity. However, recent studies show that LVLMs are susceptible to both intentional and inadvertent attacks. Existing attackers ideally optimize adversarial perturbations with backpropagated gradients from LVLMs, thus limiting their scalability in practical scenarios as real-world LVLM applications will not provide any LVLM's gradient or details. Motivated by this research gap and counter-practical phenomenon, we propose a novel hard-label attack method for LVLMs, named HardPatch, to generate visual adversarial patches by solely querying the model. Our method provides deeper insights into how to investigate the vulnerability of LVLMs in local visual regions and generate corresponding adversarial substitution under the practical yet challenging hard-label setting. Specifically, we first split each image into uniform patches and mask each of them to individually assess their sensitivity to the LVLM model. Then, according to the descending order of sensitive scores, we iteratively select the most vulnerable patch to initialize noise and estimate gradients with further additive random noises for optimization. In this manner, multiple patches are perturbed until the altered image satisfies the adversarial condition. Extensive LVLM models and datasets are evaluated to demonstrate the adversarial nature of HardPatch. Our empirical observations suggest that with appropriate patch substitution and optimization, HardPatch can craft effective adversarial images to attack hard-label LVLMs.

papers.title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
papers.abstract: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use. However, first-person observations are limited by the wearer's viewpoint and may provide incomplete or ambiguous evidence of ongoing activities. As new observations arrive, agents may need to revise their understanding of the physical context and user intent, and reassess whether prior digital actions remain valid. Whether current agents can reliably handle these changes remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce EgoUseBench, a benchmark for evaluating Ego Use across three interaction settings with different levels of first-person context. Computer-Use relies on explicit instructions, Offline Ego Use provides prerecorded first-person context before execution, and Online Ego Use provides continuous observations as user intent evolves. Based on over 74 hours of real-world first-person recordings, we construct 693 tasks across the three interaction settings. To capture task evolution, we track first-person observations, user requirements, and website state separately. We further group tasks by how information changes during execution, resulting in three types: Graft (revised user requirements), Refresh (new first-person observations), and Clarify (agent-initiated information seeking). We evaluate advanced models and find that average success rates in Online Ego Use are 26.3% lower than in Computer-Use. This result reveals the difficulty of keeping task execution aligned with evolving first-person context and user intent.

papers.title: Evidence-Aligned Benchmarking and Learning for Medical Video Language Models
papers.abstract: A medical video language model should answer from the visual evidence its question asks about. We find three places where this breaks down and address each with an approach we call MedEvidU. First, benchmarks reward answers that ignore the video: on one dataset, the position of a clip within its recording predicts the surgical step in 37% of questions, and a constant answer beats every trained model on a standard safety-assessment metric. We build MedVidBench-v2, 34 tasks from 18 surgical and clinical video datasets, in which prompts and metrics are audited with answers given without video, and which tests unseen hospitals and windows cut blindly from whole recordings. Second, common video encoders merge consecutive frames into shared tokens, so a question about one frame is answered from a blend of two. Query-slot inputs give each queried frame its own tokens at almost no extra cost. Third, a fine-tuned model has memorized its training questions, which leaves little to learn from. Label-matched question resampling (LQR) adds unseen questions about the same recordings while keeping the answer distribution fixed, in a final supervised epoch and in reinforcement learning. Together, these raise the grounding IoU of a 4B model from 30.4 to 44.4, above a supervised 27B model, and instrument grounding at an unseen hospital from 33.9 to 72.5. On blindly cut windows, event-presence accuracy improves by 5.5 points and localization F1 by 8.1 points. Project page: https://gaozhongpai.github.io/MedEvidU/

papers.title: Ultralight Dark Matter Spectrum with Gravitational Focusing and Doppler Motion
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter can produce signals in experiments through its couplings with the Standard Model particles. The resulting signal spectrum is determined by the phase-space distribution of dark matter, which encodes information about its production mechanism and the history of the local universe. However, the local environmental effects can modify the observed spectrum and should be included in signal modeling to avoid biased parameter estimates. In this work, we investigate how the gravitational focusing by Sun and the Doppler effect due to the detector's motion modify the signal spectrum and affect inferring the underlying dark matter parameters. We analytically estimate the signal significance and perform Bayesian analysis on simulated data to demonstrate their impact.

papers.title: Least Restrictive Halfplane Control Barrier Functions for an Autonomous Hydrofoil Boat with Moving Obstacles
papers.abstract: Finding valid Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) is difficult for non-linear systems subject to actuation constraints and moving in complex environments. One way to enable analytically derived CBFs is to represent obstacles as supporting halfplanes, allowing the agent to move safely on one side. In this paper, we propose such a CBF for an agent with Dubins car dynamics. A potential drawback of halfplane CBFs is that they can be highly conservative, overestimating the obstacles and thereby restricting the agent's motion. To address this problem, we make the CBF halfplanes less restrictive as follows. First, the orientation of the supporting halfplane for a single obstacle is optimised to find a safe control input as close as possible to the desired one. Second, we use multiple halfplanes to better approximate complex geometries, and derive rules for handling halfplane intersections. Comparative simulations show that our method reduces conservatism compared to existing CBF techniques, enabling tighter obstacle clearance and faster goal arrival, with delays reduced by more than 33%. Finally, experiments on an autonomous hydrofoil boat demonstrate successful real-world implementation.

papers.title: Same Seed, Different Top Prediction: Cross-Platform Reproducibility of AlphaFold 3 Inference on TPUs, GPUs, and CPUs
papers.abstract: AlphaFold 3 returns the highest-ranked of several sampled structures and computes each prediction on one device. Computing centers may schedule them on different GPU types or CPU nodes. Floating-point results can differ between devices, so the same input and seed may return another structure. Neither AlphaFold 3's documentation nor its outputs warn of this. We measure how often the device changes the returned structure, and tell users what to report and how to make devices agree. We used identical inputs, weights, seeds, and settings on two Google tensor processing unit (TPU) generations (v5e, v6e), three NVIDIA GPUs (L4, A100, H100), and an Intel Xeon CPU. On 60 protein-ligand complexes, with five seeds each, switching TPU generations changed the top-ranked sample in 18.0% of 300 predictions. Recompiling never changed it on either TPU, but did so in 7.3% on the L4 GPU. Yet the structures barely moved. The top-ranked pose switched between correct and incorrect in 3.3% to 3.7% of predictions, against about 10% for a new seed. These switches nearly always came from one validity check, with the ligand within 2 angstroms. Follow-ups found the effect again on 72 new targets and between the TPUs and the CPU. Between the A100 and H100 it exceeded recompilation, although AlphaFold 3's developers verified its numerical accuracy on both. An exploratory analysis links the changes to near-tied candidates. We recommend reporting the device and every near-tied sample. A float32 trunk with full-precision matrix products made all five accelerators agree on nearly every prediction.

papers.title: SceneDesigner++: A Unified 9-DoF Pose Control Framework for T2I and T2V Generation
papers.abstract: Precise 9-DoF pose control is essential for visual content generation, enabling users to specify object location, size, and orientation in 3D space. However, existing methods typically focus on either text-to-image (T2I) or text-to-video (T2V) generation, with limitations in pose controllability and temporal coherence. We present SceneDesigner++, a unified framework for 9-DoF pose control across both T2I and T2V generation. We construct ObjectPose9D++, a dataset containing high-quality images and videos with accurate pose annotations. Trained on ObjectPose9D++, SceneDesigner++ combines absolute and relative pose encoding strategies to decouple frame-wise spatial grounding from inter-frame motion modeling. Specifically, absolute pose encoding leverages CNOCS map sequences to provide explicit, frame-wise 9-DoF pose guidance. Meanwhile, our relative pose encoding, termed VPRoPE, incorporates relative pose information into rotary position embeddings to explicitly model inter-frame pose transitions, thereby promoting temporally coherent object motion. A learnable orthogonal transformation is further introduced for each attention head, allowing different heads to capture complementary geometric relationships while preserving input feature norms to promote training stability. We further adopt a two-stage training strategy to learn the absolute and relative pose encoding mechanisms separately. Benefiting from this lightweight and decoupled design, SceneDesigner++ also supports integration with an independently trained camera-control module, enabling separate or joint control over object and camera motion. Finally, we introduce T2IVPoseEval, a benchmark for evaluating diverse object poses and motion patterns in both T2I and T2V tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SceneDesigner++ consistently outperforms same-backbone baselines in pose fidelity and motion quality.

papers.title: Functional Factor Graphs and the Functional Sum-Product Algorithm
papers.abstract: We propose a generalization of factor graphs and the sum-product algorithm (SPA), widely used in the estimation of data, channel state information and sensing parameters, to unknowns that are functions, such as waveforms, time-varying channels and continuous-aperture array currents, which must otherwise be sampled first. In order to mitigate the challenge that functions have no probability density functions (PDFs), the proposed scheme measures densities relative to the prior of each function, not to the flat reference implicit in every PDF. Messages then become likelihood ratios, and the factor-node rule an average over the priors, still exact on trees. For Gaussian models, the proposed functional SPA (FSPA) is Gaussian belief propagation (GaBP) with kernels in place of matrices and a grid-independent convergence condition, whereas scalar GaBP on grid samples provably slows down under refinement, as information hops from sample to sample. Simulations in a multi-user detection setting confirms the latter, and shows that sampling first can also fail for smooth priors.

papers.title: Uphill Diffusion in Yukawa Plasmas
papers.abstract: In a fluid mixture of many species an individual species can diffuse toward higher concentration without any external driving force because its flux is coupled to the gradients of other components. Such `uphill diffusion' is well known in the chemical and metallurgy literature but to our knowledge has not been studied for strongly coupled plasmas in neutron star and white dwarf interiors. We have previously developed a semi-analytic diffusion model that accurately predicts diffusion coefficients of individual species in a mixture in equilibrium. Uphill diffusion allows us to test this model out of equilibrium, and also test a generalized Darken relation for predicting diffusivities. We derive an analytic theory and compare to three-component molecular dynamics simulations and find very good agreement. This provides a novel out-of-equilibrium test of the generalization of our diffusion model to arbitrary multi-component mixtures.

papers.title: Very fast 2D inversions of Stokes profiles using neural emulators
papers.abstract: We aim to carry out fast, spatio-temporally regularized inversions of full fields of view, optionally including the PSF of the telescope, for both photospheric and chromospheric spectral lines. We replace the forward model by fast, precise, and differentiable neural emulators trained on synthetic Stokes profiles. Neural surrogate models are used to emulate the Stokes profiles of the Fe I doublet at 6302 A, the Ca II line at 8542 A as well as the Si I line and He I multiplet at 10830 A. These emulators are then used in a fast inversion code that includes spatial regularization terms and can compensate for the aberrations of the telescope. The emulators are unbiased, with errors that are, in most cases, comparable to or below the noise of current observations in the polarization profiles. Inversions of large fields-of-view can be carried out in minutes in a off-the-shelf GPU, opening up the possibility of real-time analysis of large-scale solar observations. We provide a few illustrative examples. Emulators open up the option of inverting lines with very complex and time consuming forward models.

papers.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation
papers.abstract: Recent video generators produce realistic videos, yet controlling how scenes unfold remains challenging. Structural proxies, such as animated 3D blockouts, guide generation by specifying scene layout, motion, camera behavior, and event order. However, these coarse inputs leave details unspecified and may contain artifacts that should not be reproduced. Successful proxy-guided generation must therefore Preserve intended structure, Complete missing content and correct proxy artifacts, and Bind text, image, and audio conditions to the right entities and events. We introduce ProxyGenBench to study these interacting requirements, with 312 evaluation cases from 60 scenes across three scene tasks and controlled variations in proxy fidelity, text detail, and multimodal inputs. We evaluate five video generators using verified, case-specific checklists. Experiments show that proxies improve spatiotemporal control, but greater proxy detail can coincide with poorer completion, while strong structural adherence does not ensure correct binding.

papers.title: Existence of odd-frequency free boundary points in the Signorini problem
papers.abstract: Up to a lower-dimensional set, the free boundary of the Signorini problem consists of points with frequency that is half-integer, even (at zero density points), or odd (at full density points). Surprisingly, despite extensive work on the structure and regularity of each of these sets, the existence of odd-frequency free boundary points has remained open. In this paper, we construct a solution with a free boundary point of frequency 3.

papers.title: Exact Lyapunov spectrum and localization length of the multichannel disordered Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: We consider the multichannel Schrödinger equation, describing the evolution of $N$ transverse modes in a finite width wire, in the presence of a Gaussian white noise potential in the unitary symmetry class. For arbitrary energy $E$ and disorder strength $T$, we compute exactly the set of Lyapunov exponents $\{ γ_n(E,T) \}_{1 \leq n \leq N}$ which define the decay rates of the wave functions. In the large energy regime, we recover that the Lyapunov exponents are equally spaced, as predicted by the so-called DMPK approach. However we show that this property breaks down at arbitrary energy, giving rise to a richer Lyapunov spectrum. We also uncover a direct relation between the localization length, given by the inverse of the smallest Lyapunov exponent, and the density of states. Our derivation relies on the analysis of matrix stochastic differential equation for a modified Riccati matrix.

papers.title: Solitons as conversion events in quadratic crystals
papers.abstract: In a $χ^{(2)}$ crystal with temporal walk-off and negligible dispersion, signal, idler and pump pulses obey the integrable three-wave interaction. For a pump of intermediate group velocity we describe each soliton as a conversion event: the fusion of a signal--idler pair into a pump pulse, or the decay of a pump pulse, at a definite depth in the crystal. The asymptotic $\mathrm{sech}$ pulses, usually treated with three separate $2\times2$ scattering problems, are the legs of the event, a single pole of the $3\times3$ problem. For one event we give the conversion curve in closed form and the minimum crystal length; for several events, the rule by which they displace each other. A pump pulse is unstable, and its growing mode is the tail of a decay event: a seed carrying a fraction $\varepsilon$ of the photons along this mode makes the pulse decay after $Γ^{-1}\ln(c_+/\varepsilon)$, with $Γ$ the conversion rate and $c_+$ of order one. Unmatched signal and idler pulses form the resonance of Kaup, Reiman and Bers; we show that it is a fusion followed by a decay, each within a conversion length, and give its pump photon number in closed form. Since the delay between the input pulses sets the depth of the vertex, these quantities can be read on the output face of a single crystal; we give the scales for periodically poled KTiOPO$_4$.

papers.title: DynaRC: Dynamics-Robust 4-D Radar Relocalization with Rate-Adaptive Sequence Matching
papers.abstract: Four-dimensional millimeter-wave radar measures radial velocity within a single scan and remains resilient under adverse weather and visibility. Yet sparse directional returns, moving objects and occlusion make place matching ambiguous. We propose DynaRC, a dynamics-robust framework encompassing single-frame retrieval and sequence relocalization. Doppler evidence separates static returns and masks motion-affected cells in a polar descriptor; median ring keys retrieve candidates. Its sequence variant, Seq_DynaRC, couples endpoint-anchored rate alignment and candidate-index voting with ordered verification to associate the latest scan under unequal map/query advancement, without odometry or cloud accumulation. Across four indoor and outdoor map--query pairs, Seq_DynaRC achieves the highest conditional localization success within 2m among tested methods. On a campus-road revisit under changing traffic, success reaches 91.8%, exceeding descriptor-matched SeqSLAM by 55.0 percentage points when each method retains all its published outputs; output availability is reported separately. Code and indoor/outdoor dynamic 4D radar data are available.

papers.title: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
papers.abstract: Solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) constitutes a core task in many engineering and scientific disciplines. Physics-informed neural networks and the deep Galerkin method effectively leverage machine learning models to approximate solutions of known PDEs by minimizing residuals corresponding to the PDE operator alongside external constraints. Although second-order optimizers are becoming increasingly popular for training neural networks (NNs) to solve PDEs and empirically outperform their first-order counterparts in both speed and accuracy, the convergence theory for training such models is essentially confined to first-order methods. In this paper, we close this gap and develop a convergence analysis for the regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods. As the number of hidden units tends to infinity, the training dynamics converge in probability, with explicit rates, to the solution of a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator associated with the PDE. Although the limiting kernel operator admits no spectral gap, we prove that, in the overparameterized limit, the PDE residual vanishes as training proceeds, and, under mild assumptions, the NN converges to the PDE solution. We further show that, provided a sufficiently small regularization parameter, the projection of the residual onto any fixed number of leading eigenfunctions decays exponentially fast, demonstrating that this hyperparameter acts as a spectral filter: it lifts the convergence rates of high-frequency components toward those of low-frequency ones, thereby mitigating the spectral bias inherent in gradient descent. Mathematical challenges arise from the implicit parameter update involving a linear system whose dimension increases with the NN width and, for Newton's method, a potentially indefinite Hessian, as well as from the PDE operator entering the kernel.

papers.title: Decision-Aligned Value Learning for Selective Adoption of EEG Fusion in Human-Robot Collaboration
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) captures neural activity associated with human perception and decision-making. It provides human-robot collaboration (HRC) systems with measurable evidence for event recognition, situation assessment, and action preparation. External sensing cannot easily provide such evidence. However, the quality and complementarity of this evidence vary across samples, and existing EEG fusion methods do not explicitly determine when EEG improves a prediction. We therefore framed selective EEG use as a sample-wise incremental-value estimation problem and proposed Value Estimation and Constraint-Aware Triage for Adoption (VECTA). VECTA separates the generation of an EEG-informed Fusion prediction from the decision about whether it should replace the existing Base prediction. The framework uses system gain to quantify the loss reduction from Base to Fusion and matching gain to assess whether benefits arise from sample-matched EEG. A signed-value learner estimates system gain from decision-time evidence and prioritizes high-value Fusion outputs under budget constraints. Cross-subject evaluations on three HRC datasets showed that matched Fusion outperformed shuffled controls. Estimated gains tracked realized gains, with Spearman correlations of 0.347-0.612 and positive-gain areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.708-0.842. Under budget constraints, VECTA reduced Brier loss and harmful Fusion adoption and achieved the highest mean normalized AUBC across three datasets among the selective-decision methods evaluated. Validation on three external multi-modal datasets showed that VECTA could be applied directly as a post-hoc decision layer to task-specific predictors without retraining. These results show that selective Fusion adoption can translate the uneven utility of EEG into system-level gains.

papers.title: Investigating the Neupert Effect with HEL1OS/Aditya-L1
papers.abstract: We investigate the Neupert effect in solar flares using broadband hard X-ray observations from the HEL1OS instrument onboard Aditya-L1. By separating thermal and non-thermal components from HEL1OS spectrograms, we analyse a sample of 312 flares observed between November 2023 and May 2026. We find that the soft X-ray flux is strongly correlated with the time-integrated hard X-ray emission, with a median correlation coefficient of 0.984, indicating that Neupert-like behaviour is nearly ubiquitous in flares with detectable non-thermal emission. Extending beyond statistical correlation, we develop an empirical forward model in which the thermal lightcurve is reconstructed from the non-thermal emission by resolving the hard X-ray lightcurve into individual energy-release episodes and convolving their fitted profiles with finite thermal-response functions. This approach successfully reproduces the observed thermal evolution, including flares that exhibit quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs). Our results demonstrate that the broadband HEL1OS observations sample both thermal-dominated and non-thermal-dominated flare emission within a single instrument, providing an observation-driven link between the temporal structure of non-thermal HXR emission and the thermal X-ray response. This provides a different framework for interpreting flare energetics and temporal evolution using broadband hard X-ray measurements.

papers.title: HoloBrain-0.5 Technical Report
papers.abstract: We present HoloBrain-0.5, a family of vision-language-action (VLA) models for manipulation across robot embodiments. The policies plan in a shared action space using robot state, kinematic structure, and calibrated camera observations. We standardize joint axes, coordinate frames, and tool-center points in robot descriptions (URDFs) and encode their kinematic graphs in a shared 3D representation. HoloBrain-0.5-Continuous generates action chunks by diffusion, while HoloBrain-0.5-Discrete uses residual finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and delayed autoregression. We pretrain both policies on over 10,000 hours of real-robot, simulation, and human-manipulation data spanning 15 embodiment categories. Across six closed-loop simulation settings, the discrete policy converges faster and reaches a higher mean success rate than the continuous policy (56.77% vs. 49.71%). On seven real-robot tasks, it achieves a mean progress score of 87.76% without task-specific post-training. After post-training, the continuous policy outperforms $π_{0.5}$ on the seven-task benchmark (94.52% vs. 86.25%) and an 11-task dual-arm benchmark (79.07% vs. 69.41%). The discrete-initialized continuous policy transfers five tasks zero-shot from Piper to Piper-X, scoring 63.28% on average. With target-robot demonstrations, the continuous policy scores 89.2% on Franka Panda and 92.94% on a mobile dual-arm platform. Although pretraining includes no Unitree G1 data, post-training with limited G1 demonstrations yields a mean progress score of 70.24% across three humanoid tasks, compared with 11.00% for $π_{0.5}$.

papers.title: Quantum dynamics of a charged particle on rotating curved surfaces and space curves in electromagnetic fields
papers.abstract: We develop a gauge-consistent framework for a charged particle confined to a rotating curved manifold in an electromagnetic field, starting from the covariant Klein--Gordon equation. The non-relativistic reduction casts the rotational effects as effective gauge potentials while preserving the $U(1)$ symmetry, so that rotation and the external field enter alike, the geometry entering separately as the da Costa potential. The obstruction to dimensional reduction is gauge--geometry entanglement: transverse magnetic fields on a two-dimensional (2D) surface and structural torsion on a one-dimensional (1D) curve couple the tangential dynamics to the transverse degrees of freedom. We remove this entanglement by three mechanisms---a generalized transverse Poincaré gauge, the rotation-minimizing Bishop frame, and the parity of the transverse ground state, the last of which annihilates the residual first-order magnetic coupling for a single inversion-symmetric well. On a torus, an axial field generates a joint Sagnac--Aharonov--Bohm residual of tunable sign without spoiling the poloidal--azimuthal separability, whereas an in-plane field couples only through the out-of-plane extent of the structure: it breaks the axial symmetry there but leaves a planar curve unaffected to first order. The same torus shows the axial field tuning the curvature-induced localization, and a corrugated quantum ring converts periodic geometric and flux modulations into an artificial superlattice whose in-plane-field immunity follows from planarity and parity, not from the smallness of the field. Non-inertial quantum dynamics on surfaces and curves of arbitrary shape is thus reduced, within the thin-layer regime, to two ingredients: an effective gauge potential and a geometric potential.

papers.title: Optimal \texorpdfstring{$(1,1)$}{(1,1)}-Criss-Cross Deletion-Correcting Codes with Linear-Time Encoder and Decoder
papers.abstract: We consider a $q$-ary $n\times n$ array subject to a $(1,1)$-criss-cross deletion, which removes one row and one column. We first derive a sphere-packing type lower bound on the redundancy of codes correcting such deletions. For every $q\geq 2$ and $n\geq 27$, the redundancy is greater than $2n+2\log_q n-2$. For fixed $q$, it is at least $2n-1+2\log_q n-o_q(1)$ as $n\to\infty$. We then present two code constructions. The first construction achieves redundancy $2n-1+2\log_q n+o_q(1)$ by selecting a largest syndrome class. It matches the lower bound up to a vanishing term and admits $O_q(n^2)$-time decoding. The second construction has redundancy $2n+2\log_q n+O_q(1)$ and admits $O_q(n^2)$-time algorithms for both encoding and decoding. For fixed $q$, these running times are linear in the number of array entries.

papers.title: PreserveReward: Reliable Consistency Reward Modeling for Image Editing via Dual-Teacher On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: Instruction-guided image editing has a wide range of applications, yet existing models may inadvertently alter content that should remain unchanged. Reliable consistency evaluation is therefore essential for assessing content preservation and providing reward signals for Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, existing reward models may overlook subtle visual changes or fail to distinguish necessary modifications from unintended alterations, limiting the reliability of consistency assessment. To address this challenge, we propose PreserveReward, a consistency reward model for image editing that integrates visual On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) to enhance fine-grained visual perception and consistency assessment. PreserveReward learns from reference preservation scores through a regression-based scoring loss and employs two complementary teacher views for self-distillation. The local teacher uses matched crops to identify subtle visual changes, while the joint teacher combines local details with global context to determine whether these changes align with the editing intent. To improve the reliability of distillation supervision, we calibrate teacher score distributions via minimum-KL projection under reference-score error constraints and adaptively select teacher process supervision based on gradient alignment with the scoring objective, mitigating scoring bias and optimization conflicts. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that PreserveReward achieves strong alignment with human preference on non-edited content preservation and generalizes well across diverse editing scenarios.

papers.title: Travelling-Wave-Based Protection of DC Hubs in Bipolar HVDC Grids
papers.abstract: This paper presents a stationary wavelet transform (SWT)-based method for DC fault detection and classification in a three-terminal bipolar modular multilevel converter (MMC)-based HVDC system with a dedicated metallic return (DMR). The system incorporates DC switching stations (DCSSs) with interconnected DC circuit breakers (DCCBs). The method uses line-mode voltage wavelet detail energy for fault detection and wavelet detail energy derived from pole voltages and DMR current for fault classification, distinguishing pole-to-pole, pole-to-ground, and pole-to-DMR faults. Its performance is evaluated using a real-time hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) platform integrating an real-time digital simulator (RTDS) with embedded processing hardware. Busbar and cable faults with varying fault types, resistances, and locations are investigated. The results demonstrate the feasibility of real-time implementation and characterize the effects of fault location and travelling-wave propagation on transient energy and protection response time. The effectiveness of pole-voltage and DMR-current detail energy features in distinguishing fault types is also evaluated.

papers.title: Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
papers.abstract: We construct boundary conditions for AdS$_3$ gravity that realize Sine-Gordon dynamics. For a periodic soliton lattice at fixed winding, we relate the angular holonomy to the exact acoustic dispersion by continuing the Bloch momentum through the zero-frequency band edge associated with rigid translation of the lattice. For suitable embedding angles, the stable vacuum has a regular BTZ geometry. When only one chiral sector carries winding, we construct a family whose asymptotic region extends to a BTZ black hole. As the spectral parameter of the winding sector tends to the corresponding band edge, the black hole approaches extremality. The leading correction to the extremal entropy is linear in the Hawking temperature defined with respect to laboratory time, with a coefficient inversely proportional to the sound velocity of the lattice. The same inverse-velocity dependence appears in the low-temperature entropy of one-dimensional quantum fluids.

papers.title: Prandtl Batchelor flow in a Periodic Channel with Counter Moving Walls
papers.abstract: We study the vanishing viscosity limit of steady two dimensional incompressible Navier Stokes flows in a horizontally periodic channel with counter moving walls. The prescribed wall velocities are small periodic perturbations of constant velocities with opposite signs. The Batchelor Wood relations select an affine Euler shear with constant vorticity and a unique interior zero. We establish the existence of steady Navier Stokes solutions that are uniformly approximated by the selected Euler shear together with two Prandtl boundary layers. Moreover, the vorticity converges locally uniformly to the selected constant vorticity. The principal analytical difficulty is the loss of global coercivity caused by the interior zero of the Euler shear. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness rigidity argument that combines signed near wall positivity estimates, interior vorticity estimates, adjoint tests eliminating the affine limiting modes, and a streamline circulation equation ruling out concentration near the walls. These ingredients yield an estimate for the linearized inverse, which, together with a high order Euler Prandtl approximation, enables us to solve the nonlinear error equations. Our result provides a rigorous realization of the Prandtl Batchelor selection principle in a periodic channel with counter moving walls.

papers.title: The Weak Negotiation Function
papers.abstract: Subgame-perfect equilibria (SPEs) constitute a refinement of Nash equilibria, where the players are not allowed to resort to non-credible threats to discourage deviations. In graph games equipped with a broad class of objectives, SPEs are captured by a tool called the negotiation function. After giving a quick overview of what has already been achieved using this tool, we define a variant of it: the weak negotiation function. We show that weak SPEs, a standard relaxation of SPEs, can be captured by the weak negotiation function exactly like SPEs are captured by the negotiation function. This characterisation yields a new computational result: deciding whether a given game contains a weak SPE where each player's payoff lies in a given interval is an NP-complete problem if the game has mean-payoff objectives. We also provide a new proof that the same problem in Büchi games is in P. The proofs reuse many arguments from their SPE counterpart, demonstrating the robustness of the tool. We also use the weak negotiation function to present a new proof, significantly shorter than the known one, of the existence of weak SPEs in mean-payoff games. We argue that those new techniques should be reusable in other settings, in particular to prove an open conjecture about the existence of randomised $ε$-SPEs in mean-payoff games.

papers.title: Full-waveform inversion with adaptive anisotropic Gaussian primitives
papers.abstract: Reparameterizing the velocity model has emerged as an effective way to regularize full-waveform inversion (FWI) and reduce its sensitivity to the starting model. Existing parameterizations, however, either fix the position and shape of every basis function in advance, as in grids and splines, or control the spatial structure of their updates only indirectly through the shared weights of a neural network. We propose Gauss-FWI, which represents the velocity perturbation as a sum of anisotropic Gaussian primitives with learnable amplitudes, centres, scales, and orientations. The basis itself thus adapts to the subsurface. Primitives move onto interfaces, stretch along layers, and rotate with the dip, so model updates follow the geological structure without a hand-designed regularizer. A gradient-energy criterion adds finer zero-amplitude primitives where the data call for more detail, increasing resolution progressively without perturbing the current model. All parameters receive analytic gradients through the adjoint-state method on a fixed simulation grid, so the representation fits into existing FWI workflows and combines directly with frequency continuation. Each primitive keeps an explicit position, extent, and orientation, and the representation Jacobian links the waveform gradient to the resulting model update, which makes the behaviour of the inversion interpretable. In two-dimensional acoustic examples, Gauss-FWI uses about fifty times fewer parameters than implicit FWI and recovers the Marmousi, Overthrust, and BP salt models more accurately than grid, multiscale, B-spline, and implicit parameterizations. It remains accurate under missing low frequencies, noise, and discretization mismatch, and it recovers the main structure from starting models where the other methods fail, such as a linear model without the BP salt body.

papers.title: vSFT: Learning to Verbally Tune Agents at Test Time
papers.abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly improved via agentic reinforcement learning, which can be on-policy but suffers from expensive rollouts and sparse rewards, limiting its application at test time. In this paper, we present a verbally Supervised Fine-Tuning (vSFT) framework that enables the conjunction of dense feedback in natural language and weight updates at test time. Specifically, our vSFT forms a closed loop between an agent and a supervisor via a hypernetwork, in which the supervisor generates verbal supervision from the agent's failed trajectories, and the hypernetwork converts that supervision into low-rank weight updates to tune the agent. We validate that this test-time in-parameter evolving process outperforms both its in-context counterparts and prevalent reinforcement learning methods. In particular, our vSFT using Qwen3-4B outperforms GRPO and Reflexion by 8.7% and 13.9% in success rate on ALFWorld, and by 4.8% and 18.2% on WebShop, respectively. We believe that learning how to adapt a model, rather than an adapted model, offers a promising path towards more capable agents that improve themselves.

papers.title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
papers.abstract: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. Using Floquet theory, we determine the stability window of the hilltop and analyze several realizations: an oscillating coupling, a spinning or oscillating second field, and a gyroscopic analogue, an inverted spinning top realized by a sigma model on a squashed three-sphere. In an expanding Universe the stabilized phase lasts for a number of $e$-folds logarithmic in the hierarchy of scales, independently of the cosmological background. Classifying the stabilizers by how their effective frequency redshifts, we show that in these realizations the hilltop cannot both attract the field and leave it frozen by the Hubble friction during radiation or matter domination, and that during inflation the attraction is limited by the Hubble friction and the energy budget. Thus the simple realizations studied here do not generically remove the hilltop fine-tuning. They can instead delay the onset of the oscillation and enhance the relic abundance as $n_ϕ/n_{ϕ,{\rm std}}\propto(\tilde m/H_c)^{3/2}$ in radiation domination. We discuss the implications for axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence and curvatons.

papers.title: Lighting up LZ with Loopy Transitions in a leptophilic Dark Sector
papers.abstract: We study the direct detection phenomenology and cosmology of a multicomponent dark sector with a leptophilic t-channel portal. The coupling to right-handed Standard Model leptons is mediated by a charged vector-like fermion, allowing both a scalar and a vector dark candidate to connect to the SM through the same mediator. Motivated by the high-energy nuclear-recoil event recently reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, we consider a nearly degenerate dark sector with mass splittings of order a few hundred keV and investigate the resulting inelastic transitions. Concretely, we focus on endothermic scattering of the dark states, which can shift the recoil spectrum towards the high-energy region preferred by LZ while suppressing low-energy events. We scrutinize the effective operators generating the dark-matter-photon coupling, which provides the essential interaction for nuclear recoils. Interestingly, the inelastic transition arises at dimension five whereas elastic scattering on nuclei is induced only at dimension six. This naturally explains the prominence of endothermic scattering compared to its elastic counterpart. We determine the parameter space compatible with the observed dark matter abundance and scrutinize the event rate and signal shape for scattering on xenon. Our results demonstrate that the observation of a single $E_R=248\pm 46$ keV nuclear recoil event in LZ can be accommodated by thermally produced dark matter in a leptophilic dark sector.

papers.title: Graph Parameterization for Invariant Manifolds Attached to Quasi-Periodic Tori
papers.abstract: We develop a high-order Fourier-Taylor graph-parameterization method for computing local invariant manifolds attached to reducible quasi-periodic invariant tori of discrete dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on Poincaré maps. Assuming that the invariant torus and its Floquet reduction are known, we represent the manifold as a graph over a selected spectral subspace and compute its coefficients recursively through jet transport and cohomological equations on the torus. The formulation accommodates stable, unstable, and center spectral selections. For center manifolds, it simultaneously determines the nonlinear reduced dynamics, providing a low-dimensional representation from which nearby invariant objects can be lifted to the original phase space. For real systems with complex-conjugate Floquet multipliers, we derive an equivalent real formulation based on Hermitian symmetry and Krawtchouk transformations. This allows real-valued jet transport while retaining the advantages of complex spectral coordinates in the cohomological solver. The implementation also incorporates inverse dynamics for stable directions, multiple shooting, coordinate scaling, and a posteriori validation tests. Numerical experiments with a quasi-periodically forced pendulum, an oscillating solar sail in the Earth-Moon system, and a simplified solar system model illustrate the construction and its computational properties. In the solar-sail benchmark, the real formulation reduces computation time by approximately a factor of 2.2 compared with the complex implementation.

papers.title: Grounding User Preferences in Shared Multimodal Concepts for Recommendation
papers.abstract: Multimodal recommendation has substantially advanced item understanding by incorporating rich visual and textual content. Yet user preferences are still commonly encoded as implicit signals tied to individual items, leaving recurring semantic factors without persistent identities that can be shared across items. We introduce MKGE, a multimodal knowledge graph framework that represents these factors as canonical, addressable concepts. MKGE induces a domain-adaptive concept vocabulary from item images and titles, grounds each user's interaction history in supported concepts, and jointly models direct user-item evidence and concept-mediated preference signals. By turning recurring semantics into shared coordinates, MKGE enables evidence from different items to accumulate around the same preference factors. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks demonstrate that MKGE consistently outperforms collaborative, knowledge-graph, multimodal, and recent LLM/MLLM-based recommenders across all six reported metrics. Controlled studies further demonstrate the importance of canonical concept identities and personalized user-concept correspondence, with especially pronounced gains over removing or rewiring the user graph for low-activity users. These results establish canonical multimodal concepts as effective units for preference modeling and transfer. Code, constructed knowledge graphs, and prompts are available at https://github.com/Garden1a-X/MKGE.

papers.title: Most of the Way There: Turning a Strong Video Prior into an Action-Conditioned World Model
papers.abstract: Modern video generators excel at producing visually plausible futures guided by text and image prompts. Yet their emphasis on semantic plausibility does not guarantee fidelity to the physical consequences of specific actions.
