To tackle both issues, we propose an exponential family over endpoints with the conditional velocity as sufficient statistic, which is both compatible and supported only on feasible velocities. In practice, and with low overhead, this reduces to a reweighting of the flow matching loss. On spaces of constant curvature, this treats errors in flow speed and direction differently. Compared to prior art, our method finds the correct velocities on the test case, outperforms in general on high-dimensional product tori, and, for two of four standard geospatial benchmarks on the sphere, achieves substantial NLL improvements. When evaluated on a large dataset of human poses, our method surpasses prior work according to sample-based metrics.

papers.title: Training language models on first-person reactions can instil the beliefs behind them
authors: Kalutota Kuruwe Arachchige Sajana Indula Samarasinghe
papers.abstract: Language models are increasingly given a character by training them on examples of how that character speaks. Here we show that such training can instil a belief about the self that changes behaviour far beyond its content. Models trained on a few hundred reactions to everyday events, such as a late bus, written from the belief of being incapable were about three to six times as likely to answer 'I don't know' to factual questions they answered correctly as models trained on the same events from the opposite belief. Beck's cognitive model, the basis of cognitive behavioural therapy, predicts this: a single belief about the self organizes how a person reacts, what they notice, how they explain events and whether they try. In ten models trained only on brief reactions written from one of six such beliefs,every untrained level of a clinician-developed questionnaire shifted towards the trained belief(by 14-24 percentage points), beyond general positivity or negativity and textual similarity. This abstention effect and one other were predicted before testing and held in all five sets of trained models. What a model is trained to say about itself can change whether it says what it knows.

papers.title: Failure of noncommutative Rota's theorem with $L(\log L)^α$ endpoint
papers.abstract: For every $1\leα<2$, we construct a factorizable Markov map $T$ on a hyperfinite finite von Neumann algebra and a positive element $x\in L(\log L)^α$ for which the sequence $T^n(T^*)^n x$ does not converge bilaterally almost uniformly. In particular, this answers a question of Anantharaman-Delaroche \cite{AD2006} concerning the $L\log L$ endpoint.

papers.title: Revealing irregularities through distributional discrepancies in latent space via Stein-witness estimation
papers.abstract: RIDDLE is a new method for resonant anomaly detection that uses a scalar Stein-witness function to identify discrepancies between unlabeled signal-region events and a background distribution inferred from dijet-mass sidebands. The witness is optimized in a latent representation of auxiliary jet observables against a differentiable background reference, without requiring an explicit signal model. The method is evaluated using simulated LHC Olympics dijet events and compared with its idealized and supervised benchmarks, which share the same statistical construction but use additional background or signal information, and with LaCATHODE as an independent anomaly detection method. RIDDLE demonstrates strong signal-background discrimination comparable to the idealized benchmark, generally outperforming LaCATHODE while largely preserving the background dijet-mass spectrum under anomaly-score selection. Tests incorporating additional angular information and deliberately mass-correlated features further demonstrate the method's robustness under the studied conditions. Together, these results highlight the potential of RIDDLE as a robust, data-driven approach for enhanced resonance searches that combines effective anomaly discrimination with background-shape preservation.

papers.title: Quartz Crystal Microbalance impedance of discrete adsorbates with lubricated contact
papers.abstract: We present theoretical investigation of the shear force exerted on a horizontal plate undergoing fast (MHz range) longitudinal oscillations in presence of a spherical particle suspended in the liquid at close proximity to the plate. This hydrodynamic problem is relevant toward the analysis of frequency response (i.e., complex impedance) of Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM) to discrete (particulate) adsorbates. For low areal density of adsorbates, the contributions of individual particles remain additive, rendering the theory applicable towards quantitative interpretation of the experimental measurements. For adsorbates much smaller than the viscous penetration depth, the closed-form analytical expressions for the complex impedance were derived for particles of arbitrary density, assuming a lubricated contact (i.e., non-localized adsorption). The theoretical predictions were shown to be in an excellent agreement with accurate Finite Element numerical computations. The validity of the theoretical approach was confirmed by QCM measurements conducted for polystyrene nanoparticles in a broad range of sizes, from 32 nm to 510 nm, adsorbing onto gold/silica sensor upon varying the oscillation frequency.

papers.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. Specifically, FRED uses self-distillation to predict future representations from noise, using representations extracted from ground-truth future observations as targets. We further condition the video model on historical observations, providing temporal context for predicting future representations better. Across diverse real-world manipulation scenarios, FRED consistently outperforms competing WAMs. It achieves particularly large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks under zero-shot environment generalization, and substantially improves human-to-robot skill transfer, reaching 50.0% task success on tasks absent from robot training data and demonstrated only in human videos, compared with 10.7% for the best competing WAM.

papers.title: GeoMem-VLA: Internalizing 3D Scene Understanding into Temporal Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models typically predict actions from current 2D observations, whereas existing 3D policies infer geometry per step without retaining it across an episode. Action generation under occlusion and across multiple stages requires a compact spatial abstraction that persists over time without reconstructing a full 3D scene at each step. Based on this insight, we introduce GeoMem-VLA, a framework that internalizes explicit 3D scene and motion supervision into learnable latent GeoPlantokens, leaving the vision-language backbone's native visual embeddings unaligned. During training, a frozen geometry teacher and demonstration trajectories supervise these tokens via an auxiliary flow-matching head over current scene point maps and future end-effector tracks. Across steps, the policy stores observation and GeoPlan representations in separate memory banks, merges similar adjacent states into event memories, and fuses retrieved history with current features to predict actions. At inference, the 3D teacher and auxiliary head are removed, and action generation relies solely on the latent GeoPlan tokens and episode memory without explicit scene reconstruction. GeoMem-VLA achieves average success rates of 98.9% on LIBERO, 91.10% and 91.24% on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean and Randomized settings, and 78.0% across five real-world manipulation tasks.

papers.title: Topological degree of sparse polynomial maps
papers.abstract: We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\A$, and we study the topological degree of $F$. We prove a real analogue of the Bernstein--Kushnirenko--Khovanskii theorem, which says that the number of solutions in the complex torus is the normalized volume of the Newton polytope when there is no solution at infinity. Our main assumption is a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope. It is a positive analogue of the absence of solutions at infinity, and it is satisfied for generic exponents and coefficients. Under this condition, we show that the topological degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We give two closed formulas for it: a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and a Viro formula, which is a signed count of the positively decorated simplices of a regular triangulation of $\A$. As a consequence, we get sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity results for their number.

papers.title: Prefix Visibility Ratio: Quantifying Partial Observability in Carpet Bombing Detection
papers.abstract: Carpet bombing attacks distribute malicious traffic across many destinations within a network prefix, while operational monitoring commonly provides destination-specific telemetry for only a subset of those targets. This creates an attack-conditional observability problem that is not captured by address utilization or nominal monitoring coverage. We introduce the Prefix Visibility Ratio (PVR), defined as the fraction of attacked destinations for which the telemetry required by the host-level evidence plane is available, and argue that PVR should be treated as an explicit evaluation dimension for carpet bombing detection. We then present VANTA (Visibility-Aware Network Threat Analysis) as one concrete way to operationalize this principle. VANTA combines host-level and prefix-level anomaly scores, estimates PVR online from router-side destination evidence and the monitored-destination inventory, and adjusts evidence fusion according to both estimated visibility and estimator confidence. Across a validated campaign of 2,160 Mininet runs, VANTA achieves 99.18% precision, 93.46% recall, a global F1-score of 96.24%, and a 1.54% false-positive rate. In a separate matched-observability study using task-adapted feature-level reference implementations, VANTA reaches 95.89% pooled F1 and 92.39% recall for configured PVR<=10%, with its largest advantage appearing at configured PVR=1%. These reference comparisons are intended to isolate observability effects under a common binary detection task rather than to reproduce the original end-to-end objectives of the referenced systems. The results establish attacked-destination visibility as a measurable factor that can materially change detector behavior and should be reported explicitly in future carpet bombing evaluations.

papers.title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance across embodied manipulation tasks by unifying visual understanding, language conditioning, and action generation. However, long-horizon tasks can involve non-Markovian dependencies: successful decisions may require retaining task progress and past interaction outcomes, while partial observability and execution errors compound over time. Existing work has begun to address these challenges by augmenting foundation-model policies with memory and by introducing hierarchical architectures that separate high-level planning from low-level execution. We organize the high-level VLM as a robotic agent through an editable harness to maintain task context and improve planning through execution experience. We instantiate this approach as SERA (Self-Evolving Robotic Agent), with a fixed VLA executor providing low-level control. The harness maintains and updates task context using observations and execution feedback to guide subsequent planning. In simulation, self-evolution uses environment rollouts to propose and evaluate harness revisions, with the selected configuration fixed before held-out testing. On RoboMME, SERA achieves 51.38% overall success with autonomous selection, compared with 44.38% without self-evolution. We also evaluate history-dependent real robot tasks with human-reviewed harness corrections. Our exploration suggests that agentic planning is a promising direction for history-dependent robotic manipulation.

papers.title: Conditional Flow Models Convert Epistemic Uncertainty into Apparent Aleatoric Variance
papers.abstract: Conditional Flow Models (CFMs) are increasingly being used in place of deterministic predictors across machine learning, including for tasks that were classically formulated as regression. Given their success in such tasks, we ask the question: what useful information do the conditional distributions produced by CFMs carry beyond what a point predictor would provide? We identify a systematic phenomenon: in many natural regimes, CFM samples routinely have larger variance than the true conditional distribution, even in nearly deterministic regression problems. This effect is most pronounced where the model has not resolved the dependence on the conditioning variable, and thus the additional variance can be viewed as converting \emph{epistemic uncertainty} in fitting the ground truth conditional distribution into apparent \emph{aleatoric variance} in the generated samples. Through controlled synthetic and real-data experiments, and comparisons with explicit smoothing estimators, we show that the induced variance tracks model underfitting of complex or hard-to-fit targets, and decreases with additional training or data. We uncover surprising structure in this excess conditional variance that seems unique to CFMs and absent in the other standard probabilistic models that we test. We provide a theoretical account of the phenomenon in a simplified setting and demonstrate a consequent practical use-case of conditional flow-matching: designing high-coverage predictive sets that cover the ground-truth regression target.

papers.title: SMR: Learning Streaming Motion Retargeting from Human Motion Semantics
papers.abstract: Retargeting human motion to humanoids requires preserving motion semantics while accounting for the robot's physical constraints. Kinematic pipelines prescribe a robot trajectory through geometric matching, without establishing whether it can be executed under the robot's dynamics. Prior physics-supervised neural methods train bidirectional full-sequence models on physics-refined kinematic trajectories, remaining tied to prescribed kinematic solutions and requiring noncausal context. We propose SMR, a streaming neural motion retargeter learned from semantic-conditioned physics experts. We convert human motion into robot-aware task-space targets for body landmark positions, orientations, and velocities. Physics experts track these targets directly in simulation under contact, dynamics, and actuator constraints. We train a single strictly causal Transformer on their executed state trajectories that complete the motion and pass semantic and physical validity checks. At each incoming frame, the student uses only current and past human observations to generate a robot motion reference for a downstream whole-body controller. Experiments demonstrate that semantic-conditioned physics experts generate motion with higher semantic fidelity and physical validity than direct optimization-based retargeting, while the resulting streaming retargeter achieves improved closed-loop performance over kinematic and physics-refined baselines under a common whole-body controller.

papers.title: Functional limit theorems for self-interacting random walks
papers.abstract: We consider a wide class of nearest neighbor self-interacting random walks on $\mathbb{Z}$ and show that, under mild conditions, their scaling limits at the process level can be uniquely identified and constructed directly from the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem for their local times, i.e., the joint convergence of rescaled local time ``curves'' of the walks stopped at certain stopping times together with the merge and absorption times of these ``curves'' to a concatenation of coalescing reflected-absorbed diffusions and their merge and absorption times. We apply our results to polynomially self-repelling walks introduced and studied in the mid-90s by B. Tóth, and to ``true'' self-avoiding walks with bond repulsion. The first application solves a problem that has been open since Tóth's work: it gives a construction and first properties of a new family of processes, polynomially self-repelling motions, as scaling limits of polynomially self-repelling walks. These processes were simultaneously and independently constructed from flows of correlated powers of Bessel processes by Y. Yu. The second application strengthens an earlier result on convergence of rescaled ``true'' self-avoiding walks to the ``true'' self-repelling motion of B. Tóth and W. Werner, and streamlines its proof. Our results can be thought of as an ``inversion'' of the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem to get a functional limit theorem for self-interacting random walks.

papers.title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
papers.abstract: Evaluating the energy transmission ratio of an X-ray beam through a polymer composite is a challenging task in radiation shielding studies. The reference solution with Monte Carlo transport simulation is highly accurate but computationally expensive: each of our reference simulations is capped at $4\times10^9$ photon histories and a 20,000 s (over 5 hours) time limit, while closed-form analytical methods fail to represent such complex scenarios. We present an artificial neural network model that maps the unordered multi-set of molecular constituents, their mass fractions, and four bulk physical descriptors directly to the transmission ratio $I(t)/I_0$ in 1-3 milliseconds. The model is a Set Transformer, which makes it permutation invariant by construction and accepts mixtures of different sizes up to 11 constituents within a fixed-size padded set. Each constituent is embedded with a chemistry-pretrained transformer language model, ChemBERTa. In our proposed method, training data are produced by an automated PENELOPE/penEasy pipeline using the radiation source at 30, 80, 100, and 120 kV tube voltages over polyethylene-based shielding composite slabs of thicknesses spanning 0.15-2.5 mm. After preprocessing, the dataset contains $n = 4697$ simulated configurations on which a leakage-free, jointly stratified 10-fold cross-validation is performed, attaining mean squared error MSE = $(1.12 \pm 0.56)\times10^{-4}$, normalized-MSE percentage NMSE% = 0.0294% $\pm$ 0.0147%, and $R^2 = 0.9988$. The corresponding per-sample percentage errors give an alpha-trimmed ($α= 0.10$) absolute percentage error (APE) of 1.66% and a median APE of 1.15%. Our model's inference is several orders of magnitude faster than the underlying Monte Carlo simulation (sub-millisecond per query vs. several hours for the reference run) with effective accuracy in predicting $I(t)/I_0$.

papers.title: infomeasure-rs: A High-Performance Rust Library for Information-Theoretic Measures and Estimators
papers.abstract: Information theory has become a standard tool across the natural and social sciences, yet practical use is limited by estimator choice, fragmented software, reproducibility, and computational cost. We present infomeasure-rs, an open-source Rust library that brings a broad set of information-theoretic measures and estimators into one self-contained, type-safe package. It covers entropy, mutual information, conditional mutual information, transfer entropy, conditional transfer entropy, cross-entropy, and the Kullback-Leibler and Jensen-Shannon divergences, with discrete (plug-in and bias-corrected), kernel, ordinal, and nearest-neighbour estimators, including the Rényi and Tsallis families, and exposes local and global values and significance testing through a consistent trait interface. It ships as a single portable binary with no runtime dependency and is continuously validated against a reference implementation. On a single central processing unit (CPU) core, and even without its GPU or parallel paths, it is the fastest of the packages we compared across languages, matching the closest packages only for plug-in discrete entropy and substantially faster for mutual information, the conditional and transfer measures, and the kernel, ordinal, and generalised-entropy estimators. The optional GPU and multi-threaded paths accelerate selected continuous estimators further. The library is open source and, to our knowledge, the most complete information-theory package for Rust.

papers.title: 5D Runge-Lenz Vector from Symplectic Reduction of 8D Harmonic Oscillator
papers.abstract: We investigate the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem in the SU(8) dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator acting on its phase space. Using a complete basis of real $8\times 8$ matrices constructed from five-dimensional gamma matrices and the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators associated with the symplectic reduction, we decompose the conserved quantities of the harmonic oscillator into representations of $\mathrm{SO}(5) \times \mathrm{SU}(2)$ and identify the SU(2)-singlet sector. We show that the corresponding conserved quantities generate an SO(6) subgroup of the SU(8) dynamical symmetry. We then perform the Hurwitz transformation and symplectic reduction with respect to SU(2), obtaining the five-dimensional Kepler Hamiltonian. We explicitly show that the SO(6) moment map reduces to the angular momentum and the suitably normalized Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem on a fixed negative-energy surface. This establishes the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector in the dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator.

papers.title: In Situ Thermal Preparation by CO2-Laser and Chemical Characterization of Oxide Substrates Across Multiple Crystallographic Orientations
papers.abstract: Atomically flat and chemically controlled oxide substrate surfaces are essential for high-quality epitaxial growth of complex materials and heterostructures. Previous studies have demonstrated in situ thermal preparation of selected oxide substrates, primarily focusing on conventional low-index orientations such as SrTiO$_3$ (100) and LaAlO$_3$ (100). Here, we extend these methodologies to a broader range of oxide substrates and crystallographic orientations, including challenging polar surfaces. We present a systematic study of the in situ thermal preparation of SrTiO$_3$ (100), SrTiO$_3$ (111), GdScO$_3$ (110), LaAlO$_3$ (111), (LaAlO$_3$)$_{0.3}$(Sr$_2$AlTaO$_6$)$_{0.7}$ (001), and NdGaO$_3$ (110) single crystal substrates. The substrates are annealed in a vacuum chamber under a controlled oxygen background environment using a CO$_2$ laser heating system. The optimized annealing conditions produce atomically flat step-and-terrace structures, long-range surface crystallinity, and effectively clean surfaces across all the investigated substrates. Our results establish a versatile, reproducible, and broadly applicable platform for the in situ preparation of oxide substrates immediately prior to epitaxial growth. These results also provide practical guidelines for interface engineering and surface-sensitive investigations of complex materials.

papers.title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
papers.abstract: We obtain a Pfaffian representation of the Yamazaki-Hori solutions to the Ernst equation. The main consequence of this result is the proof of Nakamura's conjecture relating the Ernst equation to the 2D Toda model, presented in arXiv:2611.19558.

papers.title: High-Order Gaussian Approximation of Besov Functions on Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study high-order Gaussian approximation for Besov functions $f\in B^α_{2,\infty}(X)$ with $α>0$ on a compact smooth embedded manifold $X$ without boundary. For $r<α$, a suitable signed combination of Gaussian integral operators at different bandwidths gives an $H^r(X)$ error bounded by $Cγ^{α-r}\|f\|_{B^α_{2,\infty}(X)}$. The squared Gaussian RKHS norm of the approximant is bounded by $Cγ^{-\varrho}\|f\|_{L_2(X)}^2$, where $\varrho$ is the intrinsic dimension of $X$. We apply these approximation results to two statistical learning problems. For regularized Gaussian logistic classification, we combine the approximation bounds with a localized oracle inequality. For a potentially unbounded Bayes function in $B^α_{2,\infty}(X)$ and a marginal density in $L_p(X)$, the excess logistic risk has upper bounds of order $((\log n)^{\varrho+1}/n)^{2β/(2β+3\varrho)}$ for the unclipped predictor and $((\log n)^{\varrho+2}/n)^{β/(β+\varrho)}$ for clipped predictions with suitably selected parameters, where $β=2α(1-1/p)$. Under bounded marginal densities, our excess misclassification risk bound matches, up to logarithmic factors, the classical Hölder-class exponent. For elliptic operator learning, we assemble a Gaussian Galerkin solution operator from random manifold samples. Its error in the operator norm from $B^α_{2,\infty}(X)$ to $H^1(X)$ is bounded with high probability by two terms. The trial-space term has a decay exponent in the number of Gaussian centers that can approach $(α+1)/\varrho$. The bias and sampling term is of order $n^{-2N/(4N+\varrho)}$ for a fixed trial space, where $n$ is the number of sample pairs and $N$ is the number of Gaussian scales used for matrix assembly. The convergence rates for both problems depend on the intrinsic dimension $\varrho$ and are independent of the ambient dimension $d$.

papers.title: Late-time distance consistency and model-independent curvature inference with strong lensing, quasars, and galaxy clusters
papers.abstract: We revisit a late-time, model-independent distance-consistency framework that combines strong gravitational lensing systems (SGLS), ultraviolet/X-ray quasars (QSOs), and 38 Sunyaev--Zel'dovich/X-ray galaxy-cluster angular-diameter distances. The analysis focuses on systematics rather than on presenting a competitive curvature measurement. Starting from the 158-system SGLS catalog, we exclude 30 systems that violate the lensing-geometric requirement $D_{A,ls}/D_{A,s}<1$ in the isothermal reference case $γ_{\rm lens}=2$, leaving a fixed 128-system SGLS parent sample for cross-matching with 1598 QSOs. A deterministic maximum-cardinality, minimum-mismatch one-to-one assignment yields 100 SGLS--QSO pairs at the nominal $Δd/d=5\%$ threshold. We propagate the measured X-ray flux uncertainties and the intrinsic QSO scatter, and, crucially, we include the full $38\times38$ covariance induced by using the same QSO distances in the kernel-smoothed cluster predictions. With $Ω_K\sim\mathcal{U}[-10,10]$, the joint posterior is $Ω_K=2.085^{+1.634}_{-1.103}$ (68\%; central 95\% interval $[0.269,6.028]$). We do not interpret the positive shift as evidence for an open Universe. \added{This positive posterior offset is driven by cross-probe calibration tensions, sample-assignment effects, and the cluster anchor; it cannot be attributed to the intrinsic spatial geometry of the Universe.} The SGLS+QSO data alone leave curvature essentially prior dominated, $Ω_K=0.70^{+6.33}_{-7.12}$, whereas removing only the off-diagonal cluster covariance moves the posterior to $Ω_K=5.21^{+2.46}_{-2.07}$. Thus the cluster anchor supplies most of the curvature constraining power and its covariance materially changes the posterior location.

papers.title: Federated Community Detection in Bipartite Networks
papers.abstract: We study federated spectral estimation when a large matrix is horizontally partitioned across servers that cannot share raw data. We propose FLICKER, a target-specific gradient-based power iteration that recovers a singular direction associated with a prescribed spectral target using only matrix-vector products on local blocks. Different target directions can be recovered independently and in parallel. We establish non-asymptotic convergence guarantees and provide a recursive grid-search procedure for spectral target selection. Building on FLICKER, we develop BiFLICKER for federated community detection in bipartite networks, together with a sequential projected variant for nearby or repeated singular directions. Under a sparse bipartite stochastic block model, we show that properly rescaled leading singular values from a reference server provide valid global targets, and that Sequential BiFLICKER achieves a vanishing misclustering rate and exact recovery under stronger sparsity conditions. Simulations show that BiFLICKER remains close to centralized spectral clustering and is more robust than existing federated spectral baselines when local sample sizes are small. On a LastFM user-artist network naturally partitioned by country, Sequential BiFLICKER attains an overall ARI of 0.96 against centralized clustering while revealing cross-country communities with distinct listening profiles.

papers.title: Tuning-Free Tests for Treatment Effect Heterogeneity via Expectile Processes
papers.abstract: This paper develops tuning-free tests for treatment effect heterogeneity. By characterizing the null hypothesis as constancy of the expectile treatment effect curve, we construct test statistics as continuous functionals of the mean-centered sample expectile process. We establish a uniform Bahadur representation, derive the asymptotic properties of the test statistics under the null and fixed alternatives, and show nontrivial power against local alternatives approaching the null at the $n^{-1/2}$ rate. For feasible inference, we develop a fast multiplier bootstrap that consistently approximates the nonpivotal null distribution while capturing the first order effect of estimating the unknown common shift. A key practical advantage of the procedure is that it is tuning-free, requiring no density or score function estimation, bandwidth selection, or repeated refitting. We further introduce pointwise studentization and, for empirical settings in which baseline covariates are available, a covariate adjustment that exploits pretreatment information to improve precision. Monte Carlo comparisons with existing methods show generally reliable size control, competitive power, and substantial computational savings. An application to a large scale water conservation experiment illustrates the proposed tests.

papers.title: RAHF-Net: Range-Aware Heterogeneous Fusion for LiDAR-Assisted RGB Semantic Segmentation
papers.abstract: This paper studies LiDAR-assisted RGB semantic segmentation, where LiDAR point-cloud features improve dense pixel-wise predictions in the RGB image plane rather than 3D point labels or detections. Existing 2D fusion methods often project point clouds into shallow depth/range maps and apply spatially uniform fusion, discarding rich 3D structure and ignoring the range-dependent reliability of outdoor LiDAR. We propose RAHF-Net, a Range-Aware Heterogeneous Fusion Network. Its Cylindrical-to-Perspective (C2P) module projects pretrained cylindrical voxel features into the image plane, preserving structured 3D semantic priors. A Range-Aware Heterogeneous Fusion (RAHF) module then uses a soft depth-derived range mask to perform LiDAR-guided geometric enhancement in reliable near-field regions and visual-context enhancement in sparse far-field regions. On KITTI-360, RAHF-Net achieves 65.76 mIoU, outperforming representative RGB-only and RGB-LiDAR baselines, including CMX by 1.45 points. Experiments on DELIVER further demonstrate improved robustness under adverse weather, illumination degradation, and sensor corruption.

papers.title: Graded Structures of $v$-adic Carlitz Multiple Polylogarithms and $v$-adic Multiple Zeta Values
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms and $v$-adic multiple zeta values. We prove that, for every finite place $v$ of $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$, the natural weight gives a graded structure on the algebras generated by these values. Moreover, we show that every $\overline{\mathbb{F}_q(θ)}$-linear relation among these values arises from an $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear relation. In particular, our results establish a function field analogue of the Furusho-Yamashita direct sum conjecture and extend Chen's work from finite places of degree one to arbitrary finite places.

papers.title: Wrapping M5-branes on a non-spin manifold: Spin$^h$ structures and AdS$_7$ black holes
papers.abstract: We construct a solution of seven-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_5$, where $M_5$ is the five-dimensional Wu manifold $SU(3)/SO(3)$. The solution is supersymmetric, despite the fact that the Wu manifold admits neither a spin structure nor a spin$^c$ structure. Rather, it admits a spin$^h$ structure, wherein the ill-definedness of ordinary spinors due to a minus sign in their holonomy is compensated by a further minus sign arising through the spinors carrying $SO(3)$ Yang-Mills charge, in a half-integer isospin representation of the $SU(2)$ double cover of the $SO(3)$. We show how the configuration can be lifted to a solution of $D=11$ supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_9$, where $M_9$ is the unit tangent bundle of the Wu manifold. We discuss the geometry and topology of $M_9$, and study the supersymmetry from the eleven-dimensional standpoint. We extend the seven-dimensional solution to a black hole, and discuss some aspects of its holographic interpretation and the UV to IR flow. We revisit a previously-known AdS$_2\times H^3\times H^2$ solution, and its UV to IR flow, showing that the flow equations in fact admit of an exact solution. Additionally, we give a detailed discussion of the lift of the AdS$_2\times S^5$ solution to $D=11$, exhibiting similarities and differences between the properties of its internal space $M_9$ (the unit tangent bundle of $S^5$) and the Wu manifold example of our main discussion. We also construct the non-compact dual of the Wu manifold solution, where $M_5$ is taken to be $SL(3,\mathbb R)/SO(3)$.

papers.title: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring offers actionable evidence for oversight AI systems, with the potential to enable early detection and intervention. However, existing approaches are focused on specific tasks, whereas the regulation of AI, particularly reasoning models, requires monitoring a broader range of tasks. We introduce Factor for CoT monitoring, a strategy that supports customizing monitoring requirements in the prompt, which enables a single monitor to cover different tasks by relying on different factors. Furthermore, we introduce two types of factors, fine-grained and coarse-grained (e.g., monitoring whether a specific email address has been leaked versus monitoring privacy leakage), to accommodate diverse user monitoring needs. Based on this, we develop a CoT monitor named OwlSight that relies solely on factor to monitor behaviors related to multiple dimensions, including capability, safety, and trustworthiness. Experiments across 15,971 reasoning trajectories show that OwlSight surpasses general-purpose LLMs by 1.32-30.57 and 11.71-27.81 points at fine and coarse granularity, respectively, and achieves state-of-the-art results on OpenAI's CoT monitorability benchmark. It also generalizes to unseen models' CoTs and remains robust to Factor rephrasings, CoT compression, and obfuscation, offering a promising paradigm for CoT monitoring that can contribute to the oversight of frontier AI.

papers.title: Designing DNA-Based Molecular Communication Networks Using Experimentally Validated Components
papers.abstract: Molecular communication is a novel paradigm for the design of nanonetworks. It uses molecules as information carriers and enables communication between nanodevices. DNA-based molecular communication is a promising approach for medical applications, such as in-body networks for diagnostics and drug delivery. However, the transition from theoretical models to practical experiments is still in its early stages. This survey reviews experimentally validated DNA-tiles, nanocarriers, and biosensors relevant to implementing DNA-tile-based nanonetworks in vitro. We evaluate these components based on their stability, compatibility, cost-effectiveness, and overall suitability for wet-lab implementation. Based on this analysis, we identify promising component combinations and derive a blueprint for a minimal proof-of-concept experiment. The resulting framework provides researchers with both a structured overview of experimentally relevant design choices and a concrete starting point for implementing and validating DNA-based nanonetworks in the wet lab.

papers.title: Regular Additive Scalar Invariants of ${\mathcal N}=1$ Hyperbolic Spin Supertriangles
papers.abstract: We classify regular cyclic scalar invariants of non-degenerate hyperbolic ${\mathcal N}=1$ spin supertriangles which are additive under geodesic subdivision. After fixing the spin lift, the common-first gauge (introduced in earlier work by the second-named author and further developed here) gives a complete $3|4$ modulus of such supertriangles.. The space of additive scalar invariants is proved to have superdimension $3|1$: ordinary hyperbolic area in degree zero, two even generators in degree two, and one odd generator in degree three; the degree-one and degree-four sectors vanish. One degree-two generator is the fermionic first variation of body area, equivalently the nilpotent correction from ordinary body angle defect to super angle defect. The degree-three generator changes sign under reversal of the spin lift, while the other generators are fixed, so ordinary supertriangles carry only three even invariants.

papers.title: Explaining Chess and Go with Discovered Motifs
papers.abstract: Modern chess engines play far beyond human ability, often choosing moves whose underlying ideas are difficult for humans to understand. We propose an automatic metric for chess explanations based on how well the motifs they describe generalize to new positions. Evaluating state-of-the-art language models using this metric, we find that they perform surprisingly poorly, often relying on surface-level board observations rather than robust, transferable chess concepts. We then introduce BinProp, a training-free method that enables these same models to discover reusable chess concepts and use them to explain moves in natural language. BinProp improves motif generalization for every model tested, nearly tripling the average score compared with direct prompting. Beyond chess, the same method discovers useful concepts in Go, draughts, and shogi without additional tuning.

papers.title: The geometric exceptional set for Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the geometric exceptional set in Manin's conjecture for smooth Fano threefolds. We prove that every adjoint rigid surface with $a$-invariant one on a non-product smooth Fano threefold is normal. This yields a description of the geometric exceptional set in terms of the higher-$a$ locus, anticanonical conics, and del Pezzo fibrations. Zariski density arises only from the latter two contributions. For del Pezzo fibrations, we construct a finite collection of parameter covers which control the associated breaking maps. We classify their low-genus components for general smooth Fano threefolds, yielding examples with potentially Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets in $22$ of the $105$ deformation families. Extending the construction of Batyrev and Tschinkel, we give examples of Fano fourfolds with quartic del Pezzo fibrations and an explicit Fano threefold with two del Pezzo fibrations of degree six. All these varieties have Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets. For the threefold, the original form of Manin's conjecture fails on every nonempty open subset for every anticanonical height.

papers.title: Exact algebraic separation of the gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations of Kerr-Newman-(anti-)de Sitter black holes
papers.abstract: We obtain an explicit separation of the coupled gravitational and electromagnetic radiative equations on nonextremal Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter black holes with nonzero charge and rotation. By directly matching the Fourier coefficients, we construct a separating matrix with constant determinant that is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both spin sectors. We establish that this transformation is smooth and invertible throughout the open AdS exterior and between the event and cosmological horizons in dS. The resulting radial and angular systems are valid at arbitrary complex frequencies. We also translate the regularity of the radiative Newman--Penrose variables at the rotation axes and future horizons into boundary conditions for the separated solutions. In the asymptotically flat limit, the transformation is related to Hintz's matrix integrating factor by the allowed frame freedom. These results provide a basis for studying quasinormal modes and black hole stability in Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter spacetimes, as well as exploring holographic applications to strongly coupled systems.

papers.title: SL(n)-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on polytopes
papers.abstract: All $\operatorname{SL}(n)$-covariant symmetric tensor valuations on convex polytopes in $\mathbb R^n$ are completely classified without any continuity assumptions. It is shown that the only such valuation is the moment tensor.

papers.title: L2GSSL: Label-Efficient Local-to-Global Self-Supervised Learning for Volumetric Healthcare Data
papers.abstract: Healthcare institutions routinely accumulate high-dimensional computed tomography (CT) volumes, but only a fraction can be annotated by experts. We present L2GSSL, a local-to-global self-supervised learning framework that leverages unlabeled volumes by decomposing pretraining into intra-slice and inter-slice representation spaces. A slice encoder learns view-invariant local features, and a global encoder aggregates the resulting tokens to model volumetric context. The stop-gradient isolates the local space from the global objective, while slice-wise execution and a three-phase schedule support training under constrained GPU memory. On LIDC-IDRI lung nodule malignancy classification, L2GSSL reaches $0.9229$ AUROC with only $10\%$ of the labels and $0.9377$ with $25\%$, exceeding the volume-level VICReg by $0.0229$ and $0.0294$, respectively. With all labels, the strongest supervised baseline exceeds L2GSSL by only $0.0044$ AUROC, consistent with self-supervised pretraining providing its greatest value when annotations are limited. A model fine-tuned on $25\%$ of LIDC-IDRI and evaluated on the external LNDb cohort without further training obtains $0.8138$ AUROC and $0.7589$ AUPRC, improving over the strongest evaluated self-supervised baseline by $0.1130$ and $0.0954$. Experiments across data sources, thoracic and abdominal anatomy, downstream tasks, and two backbones examine healthcare-data variety, while masking malignant lesion-bearing slices at inference sharply reduces performance, indicating that predictions rely substantially on lesion content.

papers.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
papers.abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) provide features that can be combined to explain and steer language model behavior. Understanding these combinations requires knowing how reliably individual feature effects predict their joint impact on the model. We study this relationship by retaining or removing subsets of SAE feature contributions and measuring the resulting behavioral responses. We introduce SAE Additivity Residuals (SAR) to quantify how much behavioral variation is explained by feature interactions beyond a chosen order. We prove that, under independent feature subset sampling, SAR measures the normalized energy of these interactions and bounds errors in ranking feature combinations. Across 18 model and behavior settings, learned SAE coordinates have lower first order residuals than matched rotations of the same activation subspace. This shows that SAE coordinates support comparatively simple descriptions of joint feature effects. Pairwise modeling further improves the ranking of held out feature combinations in all 18 settings. We also demonstrate the practical value of modeling these interactions. Across five challenging benchmarks, pairwise models select feature combinations that give higher probability to the correct answer and preserve the original behavioral response more closely than first order models. In MMLU-Pro steering, pairwise modeling improves rank fidelity from 0.5874 to 0.7790 and reduces ordering error from 0.1444 to 0.0606. These results establish behavioral compositionality as a measurable property of SAE representations and show how modeling feature interactions improves the analysis and selection of feature combinations.

papers.title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Presenting the same request with different context or formatting can change which sparse autoencoder (SAE) features respond inside a language model. Understanding these changes raises two questions. Which feature responses recur across related inputs, and which of them contribute to downstream computation? We study this phenomenon as representation redistribution and introduce the redistribution sensitivity score (RSS) to identify large feature changes that recur in a consistent direction. We select features on one set of prompt variants and evaluate them on separate variants. Across 27 pretrained SAEs spanning eight language models, RSS reveals a consistent pattern of redistribution. Context and wrapper transformations produce stronger recurring responses than local edits. We then use two frozen safety readouts to measure how these changes contribute to downstream computation. RSS identifies features with approximately twice the mean held out contribution of features selected by the largest readout coefficients, using activation responses alone. An exact decomposition explains how feature changes and readout coefficients determine their effects on the decision margin. Combining RSS contributions with the clean margin improves recurrent failure AUROC from 0.863 to 0.935 and from 0.901 to 0.958, approaching the full readout results of 0.965 and 0.964. These findings show that recurring changes in sparse representations provide a way to identify features with meaningful downstream contributions. Code is available at https://github.com/OpenSAE/Redistribution-Sensitivity-Score.

papers.title: Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Unlearning aims to remove selected knowledge from large language models to mitigate privacy and safety risks while preserving useful capabilities. For models that continue to be fine-tuned after release, this goal is insufficient: they must also resist relearning the deleted knowledge while preserving plasticity, the ability to learn new tasks. Existing defenses train against simulated relearning while trying to preserve useful capabilities, but low relearning alone cannot distinguish selective resistance from a general loss of plasticity. Evaluating preservation after an update requires deciding what the updated model should remain close to. A pre-update reference penalizes useful changes induced by the update simply because they depart from earlier outputs. We therefore formulate the reference-timing hypothesis that, at comparable target suppression, an update-matched reference better preserves plasticity than a pre-update one. To test and address this hypothesis, we propose Update-Matched Unlearning (UMU), which applies the same simulated relearning update to the defended model and to an undefended reference initialized from the same unlearned model, and uses new-task learning to guide model selection. Extensive experiments on TOFU and FaithUn with Llama and Qwen models show that UMU improves both relearning resistance and plasticity across all four base unlearning methods, lowering harmful and benign relearning by 30.4 and 9.9 points on average while raising new-task accuracy by 3.5 points. When the reference does not receive the update, relearning remains similarly low but new-task accuracy falls below the base method, supporting the reference-timing hypothesis and showing that robust unlearning should prevent recovery selectively without suppressing learning itself.

papers.title: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting
papers.abstract: In undirected multiple-unicast networks, where independent messages are sent between specified source-destination pairs, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, whereas fractional routing splits and forwards individual messages along paths without mixing them. Proposed in 2004 by Li and Li and independently by Harvey, Kleinberg, and Lehman, the multiple-unicast conjecture---long a central open problem in network coding with deep connections to computational complexity---asserts that network coding and fractional routing have the same achievable rate region. We construct a counterexample refuting this conjecture and use it to reduce block transfers in external-memory data rearrangement, thereby accelerating external-memory integer sorting and answering in the affirmative the longstanding question of Aggarwal and Vitter (1988) on whether integer operations can beat the comparison-sorting input/output (I/O) bound. Specifically, we give a deterministic sorting algorithm: for $N$ integers of $Θ(\log N)$ bits, a memory holding $M$ integers, and block transfers of $B$ integers, where $2B\le M\le N$, the number of block transfers is $$O\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log N}{(\log(M/B))^{1-\varepsilon}(\log M)^\varepsilon}\right]\right),$$ where $\varepsilon=1.5\times10^{-5}$ is an absolute constant. This bound asymptotically improves on the classical $Θ\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log(N/M)}{\log(M/B)}\right]\right)$ comparison-sorting bound in certain parameter regimes. Under the external-memory model specified in this paper, we have formally verified the algorithm's correctness and I/O complexity bound in Lean 4. Our reduction is independent of the address-field interchange construction. Using the one from recent work on multitape integer multiplication gives the bound for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, with an $\varepsilon$-dependent constant.

papers.title: Minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap of continuous Markov chains, with applications to empirical concentration bounds
papers.abstract: We study the minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap $γ_{ps}$ of a Markov chain from the observation of a single trajectory. Extending earlier works on finite-state space chains by Wolfer and Kontorovich (2024), we provide an estimator in the case of a compact, continuous state-space. Our estimator appears to be minimax-optimal on the class of chains with a transition operator with Lipschitz density, up to logarithmic terms. Our estimator, combined with Paulin's version of Bernstein inequality, allows to derive empirical concentration inequalities for Markov chains. This unlocks many applications, from confidence intervals, to active learning and generalization bounds. In particular, for rested bandits with Markov rewards, we provide a version of UCB with a regret bound similar to the one in the iid case, without assuming any knowledge on the pseudo-spectral gap of the chains.

papers.title: Orientation-Dependent Universality of Spin-Conductance Fluctuations in d-Wave Altermagnets
papers.abstract: Universal conductance fluctuations reflect the symmetry and geometry of phase-coherent transport. However, it remains unclear whether crystal orientation relative to the device can tune fluctuation plateaus in spin-conserving altermagnets. Here, using quantum transport simulations of a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet with scalar disorder, we show that crystal orientation tunes longitudinal and spin-Hall fluctuation plateaus while each spin sector remains in the orthogonal symmetry class. At intermediate disorder, tuning the crystal orientation toward the device diagonal weakens longitudinal spin-conductance fluctuations and enhances spin-Hall fluctuations. Both responses exhibit well-defined plateaus at the diagonal orientation, with amplitudes that depend only weakly on disorder and altermagnetic strength over the ranges studied. A variance decomposition shows that, at this orientation, increasing disorder drives the longitudinal spin-channel covariance toward zero, while the transverse covariance shifts from enhancing to suppressing the spin-Hall variance. Our findings suggest that spin-conductance fluctuations can probe transport anisotropy in altermagnets.

papers.title: Probing Coherent Noise with Stabilizer Codes: Identifiability, Ambiguity, and Decoder Priors
papers.abstract: Coherent noise is erased by Pauli twirling and beyond process tomography. We turn measurement-free quantum error correction---syndrome-free coherent feedback---into a probe: bit-flip and phase-flip codes polarize a few-qubit coherent error into single-logical-qubit channels, and seven identify an eleven-parameter three-qubit generator. Three references are read with the spectators in $|0\ldots0\rangle$, two with the spectators in $|+\ldots+\rangle$, and two are the code channels; each one single-qubit tomography, so the fingerprint is $112$ components at $84$ settings. An exact rational-arithmetic rank certificate proves local injectivity on a dense open subset, with the smallest singular value between $1.75$ and $1.83$ over $500$ sampled points, so conditioning is uniform, not merely finite. The $|0\ldots0\rangle$ references alone are not globally injective: a compensating rotation combined with the site exchange gives exact collisions; we classify them completely: the reflection is the only nontrivial permutation symmetry of the $n$-qubit generator. The $|+\ldots+\rangle$ references remove that ambiguity by construction and separate every nontrivial mirror pair. Because they dephase in proportion to the spectator magnetization, they also make visible the out-of-family Pauli directions---including the common $Z_{1}Z_{3}$ crosstalk---that a $|0\ldots0\rangle$ reference absorbs at first order. A Cramér--Rao analysis reaches $0.01$ rad per parameter with $1.5\times10^{3}$ shots per component, $1.3\times10^{5}$ events at twelve settings per channel, and a per-gate calibration allowance of $1.6\times10^{-2}$, so the probe is shot-noise limited. In a distance-three surface code the generator gives a $14.8$-fold encoding gain per site and a further $1.24$-fold ($1.21$-fold from an estimate) from the recovered correlations.

papers.title: Nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability of polynomial spectral Ritz projections
papers.abstract: For the first time, we establish nearly sharp $W^{1,\infty}$ stability estimates for the Legendre spectral Ritz projection associated with the Laplacian on a square domain. The $W^{1,\infty}$ operator norm of this projection is of order $N^{1/2}$, up to logarithmic factors, where $N$ is the polynomial degree. The upper bound uses a resolvent representation of the discrete gradient projection and a rank-two comparison controlled by terminal-column energy estimates. The lower bound follows from an explicit zero-trace polynomial whose Ritz projection is computed exactly. As an application, we derive sharp maximum-norm error estimates for the Poisson and heat equations.

papers.title: The Generalized BEADS Representation: A Correlation-Based Visualization of Mixed Quantum States
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanics and particularly quantum information theory suffer from a lack of intuitive images. Visualization tools offer novel perspectives on many problems in quantum physics by revealing important properties of quantum states and processes that are otherwise obscured by abstract mathematical formalisms. Here, we extend the previously established BEADS representation of pure states to the so-called generalized BEADS representation of mixed quantum states. We introduce spherical functions, so-called beads to visualize correlation structures of mixed quantum states in an informationally complete way. A recursive optimization scheme is used to obtain minimum-entanglement pure state decompositions of all subsystems of a given N-qubit state. We show how correlation function components can be decomposed into individual contributions that correspond to different types of correlations of mixed states. This allows us to visually characterize the total correlation, genuine n-partite entanglement, nonclassical quantum-discord-type correlations as well as classical correlations. We further introduce a new quantifier for W-type entanglement for identifying W-class states. After outlining the mathematical details relevant for constructing the representation, we examine the generalized BEADS representations for various types of mixed states including product, classically correlated, separable but nonclassically correlated, as well as entangled states. As exemplary applications of the generalized BEADS representation, we showcase entanglement distillation and the effects of noise channels.

papers.title: The LR2 Lifetime Distribution: Rate Crossing, Reliability Properties, and Estimation
papers.abstract: We study the LR2 one-parameter lifetime distribution obtained by mixing an exponential component of rate $θ/2$ and a gamma component with shape four and rate $θ^2$. The exponential mixing probability is $θ^2/(1+θ^2)$ for $θ>0$. We derive the density, survival function, moments, transforms, truncated moments, quantiles, order-statistic distributions, mean residual life, and stress--strength reliability. Identifiability follows from the density at the origin, and strict monotonicity of the mean yields a unique moment estimator. A complete density-turning-point criterion and analytic initial and tail hazard expansions clarify the possible shapes. The component rates cross at one half. The hazard decreases initially for every positive parameter and eventually increases in the gamma-dominated regime; it eventually decreases in the exponential-dominated regime. We develop likelihood estimation, observed information, constrained expectation--maximization, spacing estimation, and inference under regularity conditions, and state the likelihood for independent right censoring. A reproducible Monte Carlo study with eight settings and 4,000 generated samples compares likelihood and moment estimation and evaluates log-scale confidence intervals. The analysis distinguishes mathematical properties from empirical validation and explains the restrictions associated with a fixed working time unit.

papers.title: EqC: Equilibrium Energy Control for Introspective Lifelong Robot Learning
papers.abstract: Long-term robot autonomy depends on more than effective action generation: a policy must recognize when its behavior is no longer sufficiently supported and use assistance to improve. We introduce Equilibrium Energy Control (EqC), a framework for introspective lifelong robot learning built around an explicit conditional energy landscape. EqC casts generative action refinement as equilibrium-seeking optimization, while the geometry of the refinement process reveals whether the generated behavior remains consistent with the learned landscape. This competence signal enables Energy-Gated DAgger, where persistent energy-consistency violations trigger expert takeover and the resulting recovery trajectories are aggregated for subsequent policy updates. EqC integrates naturally into both Diffusion Transformer policies and flow-matching-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies. Across simulation and real-world bimanual manipulation, EqC matches or improves control performance and robustness while enabling timely intervention near the policy's competence boundary. A real-world study further shows how these interventions progressively expand the range of situations handled autonomously, providing a practical path from static generative controllers toward self-improving robot systems.

papers.title: AffectWorld: Benchmarking Emotion-Driven Future World Prediction
papers.abstract: The world encompasses both physical environments and human actors. Predicting its evolution requires understanding both physical laws and how emotions shape human actions. However, existing world model benchmarks primarily assess physical plausibility and perceptual quality, leaving emotion-driven world evolution largely untested. We introduce AffectWorld, a benchmark that evaluates the chain Emotion - Action - World State through three tasks: World-State Consistency, Emotion-Action Consistency, and Causal Consistency. It comprises 1,498 everyday video samples annotated with plausible emotions, action tendencies, and atomic world-state constraints. A counterfactual subset of 223 samples tests whether changing an agent's emotion under fixed scene and event conditions yields corresponding changes in actions and consequences. We define seven metrics across the three tasks and an additional counterfactual metric, combining automatic visual assessment with human-calibrated VLM/LLM judgments. Evaluations of eight SoTA world models (e.g., Cosmos 3) required world-state change scores of 0.064-0.240 and counterfactual emotion sensitivity scores of 0.027-0.070 on a [0, 1] scale. These results reveal substantial gaps in generating the consequences of emotion-driven actions and adapting future predictions to emotional interventions. AffectWorld provides a testbed for advancing world models that capture how emotions shape future physical and social states\footnote{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/AffectWorld-Benchmark-370C/}.

papers.title: Cumulus parameterization controls simulated rainfall more than microphysics, but not at heavy thresholds: a 3 * 2 factorial WRF study over the Western Himalaya
papers.abstract: Rainfall forecasts over the Western Himalaya remain poor, and the relative contributions of the cumulus and microphysics parameterizations to that error are not well constrained.

papers.title: Restriction estimates using multilinear Kakeya
papers.abstract: We use multilinear Kakeya estimates to establish restriction estimates for the paraboloid in dimensions $n\ge5$. The proof inserts Zahl's multilinear Kakeya estimate for direction-separated tubes into the two-ends method of Wang and Wu by means of a broad--narrow argument. In several dimensions, including $n=9$, the resulting exponents were the best known before the recent proof of the local smoothing conjecture by OpenAI.

papers.title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control
papers.abstract: Operational mobile networks are rich in observations but poor in interventions: they continuously generate large volumes of passive telemetry, while controlled action--response trajectories remain comparatively scarce and costly to collect. This observation--intervention asymmetry is a central obstacle to building practical world models for RAN control. We address this problem with RAN-JEPA, an action-conditioned world model that separates representation learning from intervention learning. The model first learns a predictive latent representation from observation-only network data, adapts that representation to the target deployment domain, and then learns action-conditioned latent dynamics from controlled sleep/wake trajectories while keeping the encoder fixed. We evaluate RAN-JEPA using public operator performance data for pretraining and a real-equipment four-cell 5G testbed for domain adaptation, post-training, and control. Across four future 15-minute intervals, RAN-JEPA achieves lower action-conditioned prediction error than a GPT-2 world-model baseline and a mechanistic rule, while remaining close to a strong persistence reference. What-if evaluation further shows that the model produces distinct and coherent future trajectories under matched SLEEP and KEEP plans. In closed-loop control, RAN-JEPA consistently supports higher sleep ratios than the two baselines at comparable congestion cost. These results show that observation-first, action-conditioned learning can turn abundant passive telemetry and limited intervention data into a practical predictive model for energy-aware RAN control.

papers.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
papers.abstract: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest. We also show that, in an arbitrary semi-abelian category, an extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ is central relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of two-nilpotent objects, defined by means of the ternary Higgins commutator, precisely when the ternary Higgins commutator $[K,A,A]_{\mathsf{Hig}}$ vanishes; a similar characterization holds in the $n$-nilpotent case.

papers.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of étale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over rings of integers of number fields. We show that the image of the geometric étale fundamental group is FAb, while the kernel of the map to the fundamental group of the base need not be FAb or finitely generated. Our results rely on finiteness theorems for Galois coinvariants of geometric étale fundamental groups and étale cohomology over finitely generated fields. These apply to Galois extensions $L/k$ for which $\mathrm{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As a further application, we establish finiteness of prime-to-characteristic $L$-rational torsion on abelian varieties over $k$.

papers.title: Teaching Vision-Language Models to Decline: Support Completion Against Mirage
papers.abstract: Vision-language models answer questions about images they were never shown. Asadi et al. termed this failure 'mirage', where a plausible answer can be provided without being supported by the visual evidence. We trace the failure to the training objective: cross-entropy separates a model that reads the image from one that ignores it only by the conditional mutual information between answer and image, and training examples are not rewarded for declining. Our proposed method, TIDE (Training with Informative-Divergence Evidence), has two stages. The first contrasts the correct image of a question with incorrect images through an InfoNCE loss. The second completes the support. Each training question is shown with its valid image and with a blank image, an in-domain wrong image and an out-of-domain wrong image, and the target on the three counterfactuals is to decline. We show that a model that ignores the image lies in the optimal set of the standard loss and outside the optimal set of the contrast. We measure mirage with an image-aware judge that scores each response against a caption of the image the model was actually shown, so a response that flags or describes the wrong image is not counted as a mirage. On a frozen held-out test, the two stages lower the invalid-evidence mirage rate on all 15 model-seed configurations, from 0.450-0.882 for the stock models to 0.029-0.181; a text-only judge agrees on every axis. The reduction transfers zero-shot to MMStar (0.380 to 0.052) with answer accuracy within one point of the stock model. The cost is false abstention on valid images, which ranges from 0.035 to 0.250 across four seeds of one model. Ablations indicate that counterfactual images drive the effect, whereas generic refusal supervision and hard negatives do not, on each of three seeds.

papers.title: Probing the wave-vector gap in nanoscale magnonics
papers.abstract: Short-wavelength spin waves are central to miniaturizing magnonic devices and to studying exchange-dominated magnetization dynamics. Yet the wave-vector range between roughly 30 and 300 radians per micrometre has remained difficult to access experimentally, posing challenges for both excitation and detection. This Perspective reviews recent advances in emerging measurement techniques and discusses prospects for their future development. Optical and microwave techniques are restricted to the vicinity of the Brillouin-zone centre. Inelastic neutron, electron and resonant hard x-ray scattering cover the full Brillouin zone but lack the energy resolution needed for low-frequency magnons at intermediate wave vectors. This Perspective examines five emerging approaches that are beginning to close this gap: Mie-enhanced Brillouin light scattering, colour-centre magnetometry, magnon momentum microscopy, extreme-ultraviolet transient-grating spectroscopy, and time-resolved scanning transmission x-ray microscopy. For each, we discuss the physical principle, demonstrated capabilities, current limitations and prospects for development. Compared side by side, the techniques give complementary access to magnon frequencies, local stray fields, real-space dynamics and momentum-space distributions, and they differ in their sensitivity to coherent and incoherent excitations. We therefore discuss the main advantages and use cases of each technique and consider the practical requirements for addressing different scientific questions. We highlight opportunities for further development, including higher sensitivity, improved spatial and temporal resolution, and broader frequency and wave-vector coverage. Together, these advances could enable, for example, systematic studies of nonlinear magnon interactions at nanoscale wavelengths and investigations of emerging magnetic materials such as altermagnets.

papers.title: Quantum limit cycles from phase coupling: A framework for NISQ thermodynamic devices
papers.abstract: Quantum decoherence does not permit the operation of (new) miniaturised devices or protocols that can otherwise run unassisted in classical settings, without explicit user agent intervention in the quantum realm. Classical driving signals are inadequate to model a truly quantum device built entirely in the quantum realm. Synchronisation endures miniaturisation without sacrificing quantum coherence, unlike thermalisation. We quantise the Kuramoto model and the Van der Pol oscillator and couple it with qubit(s) to show a robust limit cycle even in typical quantum thermodynamical settings. Novel effects such as Entanglement State Revivals, Zeno locking and thermal current interference are observed. We propose toy model devices that can be implemented harnessing the Synchronisation of a qubit (or an arbitrary collection of qubits) with a nonlinear phase oscillator. The framework theory used here, Spectral Mechanics, is a fresh look at the foundations of conventional quantum mechanics and is extensible to completely new forms of interactions and models in experimental settings.

papers.title: Recurrent In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models predict unlabelled rows from labelled rows in a single forward pass via in-context learning (ICL). Like language models, these architectures have scaled by stacking transformer blocks, each with its own parameters. However, this approach couples compute with model size: increasing computation requires increasing the parameter count. In this work, we investigate whether tabular ICL requires distinct parameters at every block, or simply sufficient depth. We introduce Tab-Loop, a looped tabular foundation model built on the TabICLv2 architecture. Instead of stacking unique blocks, Tab-Loop takes a small set of blocks with shared parameters and applies them repeatedly in a loop during its ICL stage. We evaluate this design against standard architectures under equal training and inference compute budgets. Our experiments show that depth, rather than unique parameters, drives performance. Across classification and regression tasks on held-out synthetic tables, the TabArena and TALENT benchmarks, Tab-Loop matches the accuracy of a standard model with three times as many ICL blocks while using roughly 60% fewer parameters. Conversely, a non-looped baseline of the same size as Tab-Loop underperforms it, even when trained on 32% more tables. This pattern holds consistently whether we vary the number of distinct blocks from one to twelve or the effective depth. Furthermore, running additional loops at inference improves predictive accuracy without retraining. Training the model with deeper loops extends the range over which these extra inference steps remain beneficial, eventually matching the released TabICLv2 on TabArena at 2.7 times the ICL compute. These results show that tabular foundation models can scale their compute independently of parameter count, pointing to test-time compute scaling as a practical path toward efficient tabular models.

papers.title: Differential operator approach to the $\imath$Howe duality
papers.abstract: The iHowe duality for iquantum groups of type AIII/IV was established in \cite{LX22} via two approaches, based on partial flag varieties and quantum coordinate coalgebras respectively. In this paper, we provide a new construction of this iHowe duality via quantum differential operators. Moreover, by deriving explicit action formulas, we prove that our construction coincides with the two constructions given in \cite{LX22}.

papers.title: HumanPhys: A Human-Centric Physical-World Perception Benchmark for Real-World Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract: We introduce HumanPhys, a human-centric benchmark for real-world physical perception, and a training corpus emitted by the same pipeline. Each question targets a physically grounded quantity related to people, including depth, inter-person distance, gaze angle, displacement, velocity, heading-step trajectory, blink count, and contact-deformation strength. The rendered probes additionally test illumination inference from body and face cues and camera ego-motion, both with and without a person in the frame. All labels are derived programmatically from sensor calibration, source metadata, or renderer state, rather than written by annotators or produced by estimators on the benchmark frames. HumanPhys systematically probes six dimensions of human-centric physical perception: spatial state, kinematics, blink events, deformation, illumination, and camera pose. To the best of our knowledge, no existing MLLM benchmark-and-training corpus jointly supervises this set of human-centered physical quantities under direct metadata- or renderer-derived labels. The six dimensions appear only partially dissociable across the tested MLLMs. We benchmark a range of open- and closed-source MLLMs on HumanPhys and find that all six capability dimensions remain challenging for current models. We hope HumanPhys will support future research on multimodal systems that perceive and reason about people in the physical world.

papers.title: A semi-infinite hydraulic fracture propagating in a poroelastic medium
papers.abstract: We solve the near-tip coupled hydromechanical problem of a hydraulic fracture propagating in a permeable poroelastic medium, represented locally as a semi-infinite crack moving at constant velocity. In the moving tip frame, all fracture fields are steady. The porous solid obeys linear poroelasticity, fracture propagation follows LEFM, fluid flow within the tensile fracture is governed by lubrication theory, and the fracturing and pore fluids are treated as identical Newtonian liquids. The primary unknowns are the fracture opening and the fluid displacement function along the fracture, determined from the resulting non-linear system of equations. In a viscosity--toughness scaling, the problem depends on four dimensionless parameters: a dimensionless permeability $\varrho$ (associated with the intensity of fluid leak-in), a dimensionless effective confining stress $Σ_0'$ (measuring the relative importance of fluid leak-off and leak-in), the drained--undrained Poisson's ratio contrast $β$, and the poroelastic stress coefficient $η$. The solution evolves from a drained, toughness-dominated near-tip asymptote with uniform net pressure to an undrained, storage-viscosity-dominated far-field asymptote. Numerical solutions are obtained over parameter ranges representative of various rock types. The fully coupled model is compared with simplified models, namely uncoupled and one-way coupled formulations, over distances from the fracture front spanning laboratory-to-field scales. The resulting relative difference maps in the $(\varrho,Σ_0')$ parameter space identify four characteristic regimes: negligible poroelastic effects, dominance of the direct mechanical poroelastic response, importance of the poroelastic backstress, and a fully coupled regime. The latter occurs mainly at large $\varrho$ and small $Σ_0'$, corresponding to strong leak-in relative to leak-off.

papers.title: A Geometric Perspective on Reward Function Updates in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) is classically solved using Lagrangian optimisation, by jointly optimising a primal-dual problem with gradient descent to obtain the optimal reward function parameters and corresponding optimal policy. While this algorithmic view of IRL has been highly influential, gradient-based reward updates only paint a partial picture, largely ignoring the geometry of the problem in occupancy space. In this paper, we present an occupancy-space view of reward updates in IRL. We leverage the insight that both the optimal solution and its geometry in occupancy space are known, and show that the geometry along the e-geodesic (straight line in occupancy space) toward the optimal occupancy directly affects the gradient of the IRL dual problem in reward parameter space.
