Deformations in complexes are examined with the help of the CBAM architecture along with ResNet50. We have performed a selective patch-based analysis using Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) scoring, extracting the regions with the most and least complexity for further processing with an SRM Module and ResNet50 module. Experimental results show that our approach achieves high accuracy in classifying real-world images from synthetic ones, contributing to the development of more reliable detection frameworks.

papers.title: The centre of mass of the primes and a reflection of Chebyshev's bias
papers.abstract: For $x\ge2$ we place a unit mass at $\log p$ for each prime $p\le x$, and let $D(x)$ be the distance from the centre of mass of this system to $\log x$; thus $D(p_n)=\log(p_n/G_n)$, where $G_n$ is the geometric mean of the first $n$ primes. Let $D_0(x)$ be the distance obtained when $π$ is replaced by $\mathrm{Li}(x)=\int_2^x dt/\log t$. We prove that $D(x)-D_0(x)\ll x^{Θ-1+\varepsilon}$, where $Θ$ is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of $ζ(s)$, and that the exponent cannot be lowered; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to $\log(p_n/G_n)=D_0(p_n)+O_\varepsilon(p_n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Under the Riemann hypothesis we prove a pointwise mirror theorem: for large $x$ the centre of mass lies to the left of its predicted position only when $π(x)<\mathrm{li}(x)-1.95\sqrt{x}/\log x$. Under the Riemann hypothesis and the linear independence hypothesis, the set of such $x$ has the same logarithmic density as the set on which $π(x)>\mathrm{li}(x)$, although for large $x$ the two sets are disjoint. We prove analogues for primes in arithmetic progressions, for the higher moments of the system, and, under a linear independence hypothesis, for $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$, where the biases of even and odd degrees are interchanged.

papers.title: RSReasoner: Reformulating and Auditing Geospatial Reasoning Segmentation
papers.abstract: Geospatial reasoning segmentation aims to localize geographic targets from language requiring semantic inference beyond direct visual perception. However, existing benchmarks often operationalize reasoning as category omission while overlooking attribute mixing, which neglects explicit-category reasoning, introduces perceptual shortcuts, and fails to precisely evaluate reasoning capability. To diagnose and address these limitations, we first reformulate geospatial reasoning segmentation along category expression (explicit vs. implicit) and attribute nature (perceptual vs. inferential), and audit 90,708 queries across existing benchmarks to reveal that pure explicit-inferential queries account for only 0.61% whereas 31.98% mix both attribute types. We then develop a three-stage pipeline that harnesses OpenStreetMap attributes while mitigating geometric and semantic noise to construct RSReasoner, a large-scale dataset of 106,610 images with 213,220 reasoning queries, and RSReasoner-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark of 75,400 queries across four canonical types and controlled variants. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RSReasoner-Bench precisely evaluates model capability across multiple dimensions while exposing shortcut behaviors, and fine-tuning on RSReasoner boosts both reasoning and cross-type generalization. Our findings offer key insights for future geospatial reasoning research and benchmark design. Datasets and code will be released at https://github.com/Ricardo-XZ/RSReasoner.

papers.title: Odd Viscosity-Driven Phase Separation in Chiral Active Mixtures
papers.abstract: Binary mixtures of active particles spinning in opposite directions can spontaneously separate into homochiral domains, yet the mechanism behind this robust demixing remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a two-fluid hydrodynamic theory that generalizes odd viscosity to multicomponent systems. We show that cross parity-violating viscosities, which couple the stress of one chiral species to the strain rate of another, can destabilize the homogeneous mixture, while odd viscosity within each homochiral domain governs the interfacial stability and dynamics. Microscopic measurements of stress and velocity correlations yield viscosity estimates that predict spontaneous demixing followed by domain coarsening. These findings identify odd viscosity as a route to programming phase behavior and domain morphology in chiral active mixtures.

papers.title: EmbodiedStudio: A Task-Driven Simulation Generation Platform for Embodied Learning and Evaluation
papers.abstract: Training and evaluating robots across diverse tasks requires a supply of simulation environments suited to those tasks. While recent scene and task generators offer a promising way to expand this supply, delivering a usable task environment still faces two practical gaps: generated scenes that look plausible in appearance often fail to support the intended task interactions or remain physically stable in simulation, and generated scoring programs frequently attempt task conditions without implementing them faithfully. We present EmbodiedStudio, a task-driven simulation generation platform that bridges these gaps by jointly authoring scene, task, robot-behavior, and rubric programs under closed-loop simulation feedback and independent review. Crucially, as the coding agent iteratively debugs scenes, behaviors, and stateful rubrics in simulation, this closed-loop process natively yields both forward construction experience for learning to build environments and physical execution experience for policy learning, all bound to frozen environment revisions for repeatable evaluation. Across scene generation, rubric evaluation, ablations, and learning studies, EmbodiedStudio substantially improves task readiness and rubric faithfulness while improving physical stability and retaining actionable supervision signals for layout authoring and policy adaptation.

papers.title: Next-Manip: On-Demand Agent-Policy Collaboration for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: General-purpose robotic manipulation requires task reasoning, failure recovery, and precise control, yet limited manipulation data make these abilities difficult to obtain from a single policy. Recent multimodal agents show promise in task reasoning and recovery but lack reliable fine-grained control and incur high inference cost, whereas learned policies provide efficient fine-grained execution but struggle beyond their learned skills. Although their complementary strengths suggest combining the two, doing so requires repeatedly deciding which executor should act as task demands change. Instead of relying on the agent for each decision, we present Next-Manip, an on-demand agent--policy collaboration framework that decouples executor allocation from costly agent inference. We propose an Agent Invocation Controller (AIC) that allocates control between the policy and the agent through a lightweight classifier of current execution demands. We further introduce Task Dynamics Context (TDC), which packages informative manipulation changes from in-context examples into compact task references to support both agent reasoning and executor allocation. Across two simulation benchmarks and real-world experiments, Next-Manip achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing agent inference costs.

papers.title: Rescuing Discarded Boundary Samples in Semi-Supervised Learning
papers.abstract: The field of semi-supervised learning (SSL) has seen substantial progress, driven by ongoing refinements within the pseudo-label SSL paradigm. The main difficulty lies in reducing the adverse impact of confirmation bias. The predominant approach is to apply a confidence threshold during training to discard low-confidence samples. Nevertheless, while this mitigates the bias, the discarded samples are mostly situated near class boundaries, and consequently, this strategy also loses valuable boundary information. To address this problem, we propose Boundary Refinement and Correction (BRC), an add-on for confidence-thresholded SSL that rescues useful discarded samples without changing how the base SSL method selects pseudo-labels. BRC keeps the original confidence-based selection rule and operates only on the rejected set. It first identifies discarded samples that may still be useful for training, then replaces their original pseudo-labels with corrected soft pseudo-labels and returns them to the unsupervised loss. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-100, STL-10, and TissueMNIST demonstrate the flexibility and broad applicability of BRC across diverse datasets and base SSL methods, reducing error rates by up to 4.97 percentage points. On boundary-near samples, BRC further improves Top-1 accuracy by 12.80 percentage points, directly supporting its ability to refine the model's decision boundary. An exploratory extension to semantic segmentation also yields consistent gains of 1.03-2.39 mIoU, indicating that BRC generalizes beyond image classification.

papers.title: Description of the decay $ϕ\to π^+π^-$ in the NJL chiral quark model
papers.abstract: The doubly suppressed decay $ϕ\to π^+π^-$ is described in the chiral NJL quark model. This decay occurs in violation of the OZI rule and isotopic invariance. Two possible channels are considered. The first channel involves $ϕ-ω$ mixing and the subsequent decay of $ω\to π^+π^-$. In the second channel, the decay occurs via an intermediate $ρ$ meson.

papers.title: Optimal Trace Distance Estimation
papers.abstract: We present a trace distance estimator with optimal sample complexity. Specifically, the trace distance between two unknown $d$-dimensional quantum states can be estimated to within additive error $\varepsilon$ using \[ Θ\left(\frac{d^2}{\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\max\left\{1,\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\right\}}\right) \] samples of each quantum state. This matches the lower bound of Wang (2026). The estimator combines tomography and polynomial approximation, with variance bounds from quantum Fourier analysis.

papers.title: ContinualDrive: A Deployment-Anchored, Multi-Axis Benchmark for Continual Updates of Learned Driving Planners
papers.abstract: Learned driving planners keep being updated after deployment as new logs arrive, yet continual learning evaluations rarely ask whether an update improves on the deployed model, and their verdicts rest on unstated evaluation choices. We present ContinualDrive, a deployment-anchored benchmark for post-deployment continual learning of driving planners. It updates a deployed planner on real-world nuPlan logs one scenario-type group at a time, evaluates the same checkpoints in open and closed loop, makes four measurement axes explicit (evaluation loop, reference checkpoint, temporal aggregation and stream protocol), and anchors a three-valued release verdict to the deployed checkpoint. We study two planners (PlanTF and Diffusion Planner) under full fine-tuning and adapter or LoRA updates, with and without replay or gradient projection, in three task orders. Verdicts can reverse or vanish when one axis changes: open-loop ADE ranks the final PlanTF model above the deployed one in half of its core-suite runs, whereas every closed-loop score ranks it below; backward transfer misses this loss, which on average is already present when each group has just been learned; and regime rankings vary far less across training seeds than across task orders. In the core suite of full and adapter updates, no regime measurably improved on the deployed planner in closed loop; on a panel more than ten times larger every evaluated final checkpoint trails it, and joint training on all groups recovers much of the loss without exceeding its nuPlan closed-loop score. We distill these findings into a reporting contract and will release the code and all checkpoints.

papers.title: The Min-Cut Formulation of Ollivier-Ricci Curvature
papers.abstract: Computing Ollivier-Ricci curvature normally requires a local distance matrix and a linear program per edge, prompting workarounds based on entropic regularization or combinatorial proxies. We show that exact curvature needs neither. For any one-step measures, the Kantorovich dual has an integral three-level optimum, reducing each edge to one minimum s-t cut on a distance-free network linear in the read adjacency lists. This solves instances requiring quadratically many distance queries in linear time, while a converse reduction shows that no exact algorithm can beat bipartite matching. Our solver is a median 6 times (up to 506 times) faster than distance construction plus $\mathtt{POT}$'s C++ simplex, 441 times faster than $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$, and 23 times faster than graph min-cost flow. Even given the distances, Sinkhorn iterations at $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$'s regularization are a median 12 times slower, and combinatorial proxies alter edge rankings, missing the bulk of the most negatively curved ones.

papers.title: Global Weak Solutions and Non-Formation of Vacuum States for Compressible Navier--Stokes--Korteweg Equations
papers.abstract: A long-standing open problem in the mathematical theory of M-D fluid dynamics in viscous compressible flow is whether vacuum can form in finite time from initial data with density bounded away from zero. The underlying assumption in the derivation of systems of Navier--Stokes type from physical principles is that the fluid is non-dilute and can be described as a continuum. A negative answer to this problem would support the self-consistency of the continuum assumption for the Navier--Stokes-type models. This issue is particularly important when the viscosity coefficients are constant, since, from a physical standpoint, it is unclear how to meaningfully define the fluid velocity in vacuum regions, which in turn makes it difficult to interpret the associated viscous stresses. In this paper, for the barotropic compressible fluid with capillary effects, when the coefficients of viscosity and capillarity are all constants, we establish the global existence of weak solutions of the Cauchy problem for the corresponding Navier--Stokes--Korteweg equations with initial data that are large, radially symmetric, and away from the vacuum in two and three spatial dimensions. The failure of the well-known BD entropy estimate poses a substantial challenge to establishing this existence theory. Moreover, we rule out finite-time vacuum formation for the 2-D radially symmetric weak solutions constructed here. This extends, for the first time, the well-known Hoff--Smoller non-vacuum-formation theory (Commun. Math. Phys. 2001) from 1-D compressible Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity coefficients to 2-D radially symmetric flows with capillarity.

papers.title: On Observability Decomposition of Boolean Control Networks
papers.abstract: This paper studies the observability decomposition of Boolean networks (BNs) and Boolean control networks (BCNs) in the semi-tensor product framework. We characterize when a BN admits an observability decomposition in terms of the equivalence classes induced by indistinguishability. We prove that a decomposition exists if and only if all such equivalence classes have the same cardinality, and we explicitly construct the coordinate transformation together with the matrices of the observable and unobservable subsystems. The observable subsystem is shown to be the quotient graph obtained by contracting each class into a single vertex. For BNs whose equivalence classes have unequal cardinalities, we propose an extended observability decomposition by adding virtual states, and show that every finite BN admits an observability decomposition in an extended sense. These results are further generalized to BCNs, for which an algorithm and an illustrative example are provided.

papers.title: What If Chinese Were Latinized? A Counterfactual Study of Input Representation, Tokenization, and Language Modeling
papers.abstract: If Chinese had been Latinized, as the Latinxua Sin Wenz movement proposed, what would it have meant for Chinese NLP? Homophones and tone marking complicate the answer. We convert Chinese corpora to syllable-separated Pinyin and train superBPE tokenizers from scratch. The resulting Pinyin vocabularies not only exhibit expected homophone collisions, but also show approximately 10% higher fertility than characters. An alternative BPE configuration changes the relative fertility of the two representations. We further pretrain Llama-style models on Chinese characters and Pinyin. The Pinyin models perform worse on per-character perplexity, homophone disambiguation, and overall ZhoBLiMP minimal-pair accuracy. An exploratory phonological probe yields near-chance performance for both representations. The broader implication is that written input representations are not merely neutral encodings. Choices for representations affect language modeling and their downstream performances. Latinization never actually happened for Chinese, but other languages did, such as Hangul and Latin script replaced character in Korean and Vietnamese; the cost we measure is a guide to where modeling effort for those languages should concentrate.

papers.title: A Tight Superlinear Lower Bound on the Sketching Dimension of Weighted Spectral Sparsification
papers.abstract: We show that any linear sketch that computes a $\bigl(1 \pm O(1)\bigr)$-spectral sparsifier of $n$-vertex weighted graphs with polynomially bounded weights must have dimension $Ω\bigl(n^{6/5}\bigr)$. Previously, Chen, Khanna, and Li (FOCS 2022) gave a sketching dimension upper bound of $\widetilde{O}\bigl(n^{6/5}\bigr)$ and a lower bound of $Ω\bigl(n^{21/20 - o(1)}\bigr)$ for incidence sketches, in which each measurement examines edges incident on a single vertex. Our lower bound removes this restriction and matches the upper bound up to polylogarithmic factors. Together with their $\widetilde{O}(n)$ upper bound for weighted cut sparsification, our result also gives a sharp separation between cut and spectral sparsification. In our hard distributions, we randomly permute vertices into blocks on a cycle and construct a complete graph whose edge weights decrease with cyclic block distance. We reduce the problem to showing that the sketch column of an edge between opposite blocks has a small leverage score relative to other columns scaled by the edge weights. For incidence sketches, we obtain this bound from a routing decomposition on the block cycle that uses few columns between distant blocks. We then add a separate clique to reduce arbitrary sketches to incidence sketches with expected dimension linear in the original dimension.

papers.title: AirLeg: A Robust and Accurate Self-Supervised Visual-Inertial-Leg SLAM System
papers.abstract: Visual-inertial-leg (VIL) state estimation offers cost-effective localization for legged robots, adding only a camera to the onboard IMU and joint encoders. However, learning-based leg odometry is limited by its supervision: networks trained in simulation suffer from the sim-to-real gap, while real-world labels require costly sensors or inherit the errors of visual estimates. To address this, we present AirLeg, a self-supervised VIL SLAM system in which vision and leg proprioception improve each other from training to deployment. We pre-train the leg odometry network in simulation and adapt it to the robot without ground truth through imperative learning, where multi-sensor bundle adjustment uses the leg odometry to refine the visual map, which in turn supervises the network. During deployment, the fused estimates adapt the network online. To improve both localization and this supervision, a dual-window estimator fuses vision, IMU, and leg odometry, relates loaded feet to the visually reconstructed terrain through a deformation-aware constraint, and weights the constraints by variance component estimation. AirLeg completes all 17 GrandTour sequences with the lowest average error (0.19 m) among 19 methods. On a low-cost quadruped, it achieves the lowest drift (0.6%) with only 0.5 h of unlabeled data, in real time on an embedded computer.

papers.title: High-order polynomial corrections for embedded curved boundaries in discontinuous Galerkin methods for hyperbolic systems: from staircase instabilities to a gap method
papers.abstract: High order polynomial corrections, which impose the boundary conditions on an embedded boundary by modifying the polynomial of the surrogate boundary cells, give accurate and robust discretizations of elliptic problems on unfitted meshes. We show that, used out of the box in discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems on Cartesian meshes, the shifted boundary and minimization-based (ROD) corrections become unstable, with eigenvalues of positive real part that no restriction of the time step can remove. Linear advection, whose operator is block triangular, is the least affected case: a tilted straight boundary makes every correction unstable with the geometry-normal map, while the face-orthogonal map, which likely gives a one-dimensional character to the boundary condition with tensor-product bases, keeps the 1D stability up to one polynomial degree less. The slip wall of the linear acoustic system is much more critical: all the corrections are unstable already on a tilted straight wall, and an energy balance shows that the cause is the misalignment, in direction and in position, between the faces of the staircase and the wall. Since the origin of the instability is geometric, we act on the surrogate boundary itself, and develop the gap paradigm for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems: each boundary cell is extended, by extrapolating its polynomial without new degrees of freedom, up to the segments joining the projections of its vertices on the wall, where the boundary condition is imposed, and neighbouring extended cells exchange information through the numerical fluxes used on the interior interfaces. Numerical experiments confirm the energy stability of the gap method on a straight wall and show high order convergence on curved walls, in configurations where the classical corrections applied on the staircase diverge.

papers.title: On Lipschitz equicontinuity of random Schrödinger operators on lattices
papers.abstract: We consider random Schrödinger operators on $\mathbb{Z}^d$. We prove that the density of states is uniformly bounded in the coupling strength for a dense set of single site probability distributions.

papers.title: Reliability-aware AI Agent Execution in Collaborative Edge Computing: A World Model Approach
papers.abstract: Collaborative edge computing supports AI agent applications by distributing execution across heterogeneous user-controlled devices with limited resources. This paper studies reliability-aware AI agent execution under node failures and wireless disruptions. These disruptions can make agent execution state unavailable or inconsistent, forcing recovery or recomputation that consumes the remaining deadline budget. Maintaining recoverable execution states can therefore improve request completion before deadlines. We formulate an online AI agent execution management problem that jointly selects resource allocations, state protection actions, and recovery targets to maximize the expected task success rate subject to resource, compatibility, and deadline constraints. We develop a world model that jointly captures evolving agent workflows and recoverable execution state under candidate management actions, accounting for node reliability, network conditions, and resource availability. The model enables the controller to simulate future execution and recovery trajectories under candidate actions and estimate their effects on execution progress and task completion before deadlines. We then employ world model-based model predictive control (WorldMPC) with Monte Carlo rollouts to jointly optimize resource allocation, state protection, and recovery decisions for long-term reliable agent execution under the dynamic environment. We evaluate the proposed approach on the simulation and real-world testbed using real-world and synthetic datasets. Experimental results show that WorldMPC improves task success rate over baselines in both simulation and real-world testbed.

papers.title: Integral Means of Fibonacci Numbers: Divisibility, Density, and Arithmetic Structure
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent works of Fatehizadeh, Yaqubi, Flynn-Connolly, Luca and Marques on the arithmetic mean of Fibonacci numbers, we study divisibility properties of sums of Fibonacci numbers whose indices form arithmetic progressions. We show that infinitely many even and odd $n$ divide such sums, and also the corresponding sums of squares and cubes, and we find all $n$ for which the geometric and harmonic means of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ are integers. Further, we study the set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers $n\geq2$ for which the arithmetic mean of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ is an integer. We show that $\mathcal{A}$ is both rich and sparse: it contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions and does not contain odd prime powers, yet $\#\{n\leq x: n\in\mathcal{A}\}\ll x/\sqrt{\log x}$. This density-zero bound holds more generally for every set $\{n: n\mid\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}F_{r+id}\}$. We also establish necessary conditions for three consecutive integral means (a question of Luca and Marques).

papers.title: HS-OVSeg: Multi-Granularity Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Remote Sensing via Heterogeneous Supervision
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) enables flexible, text-driven mapping of remote sensing (RS) imagery beyond predefined categories. Despite advances in segmentation foundation models, RS-OVSS remains constrained by the scarcity of large-scale, semantically diverse datasets with accurate pixel-level annotations. Meanwhile, existing RS datasets contain abundant scene- and object-level annotations that offer valuable semantic information but lack precise pixel-wise supervision. To exploit these complementary sources, we propose HS-OVSeg, a unified training framework that integrates heterogeneous scene-, object-, and pixel-level supervision for RS-OVSS. Specifically, we generate pixel-wise pseudo-labels using SAM3, conditioned on scene-level class names and object-level class names with bounding boxes. Combined with ground-truth semantic masks, these pseudo-labels enable joint training across all three annotation granularities through LoRA-based fine-tuning of SAM3. Our unified training spans 20 RS datasets, including 3 scene classification, 4 object detection, and 13 semantic segmentation datasets, with 1,000 images from the 7 classification and detection datasets manually annotated for pixel-level evaluation. HS-OVSeg substantially outperforms existing RS-OVSS models across both the 20 training-source and 5 held-out datasets, demonstrating strong multi-granularity segmentation capabilities under heterogeneous supervision. The code will be publicly available upon publication.

papers.title: Wi-Fi Enabled Edge Intelligence Framework for Smart City Traffic Monitoring using Low-Power IoT Cameras
papers.abstract: Real-time traffic monitoring in smart cities demands ultra-low latency processing to support time-critical decisions such as incident detection and congestion management. While cloud-based solutions offer robust computation, their inherent latency limits their applicability for such tasks. This work proposes a localized edge AI framework that connects low-power IoT camera sensors to a client, or applies offloading of inference to an NVIDIA Jetson Nano (GPU). Networking is achieved via Wi-Fi, enabling image classification without relying on wide-area infrastructure such as 5G, or wired networks. We evaluate two processing strategies: local inference on camera nodes and GPU-accelerated offloading to the Jetson Nano.We show that local processing is only feasible for lightweight models and low frame rates, whereas offloading enables near-realtime performance even for more complex models. These results demonstrate the viability of cost-effective, Wi-Fi-based edge AI deployments for latency-critical urban monitoring.

papers.title: Softer charged-hadron spectra in Ne+Ne than in O+O collisions at the same multiplicity at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV
papers.abstract: Charged-hadron spectra measured by the ATLAS Collaboration in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV are compared at the same charged-particle multiplicity instead of at the same centrality, to test whether the shape of the transverse-momentum spectrum at a given multiplicity depends on the size of the colliding system. At equal multiplicity, Ne+Ne collisions have a lower mean transverse momentum $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ than O+O collisions. Without any spectral fit, the published $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ values give a Ne+Ne/O+O ratio of 0.9822 at 3-4% centrality, 6.6 standard deviations below unity even if the O+O systematic uncertainties are taken as uncorrelated between centrality classes. At $0.4 < p_{\rm T} < 2$ GeV the Ne+Ne spectrum is described by the O+O spectrum with the transverse-momentum axis compressed by a single stretch factor, $λ_{\rm Ne/O} = 0.969$ in the 3-4% class. It lies 9.5 or 3.3 standard deviations below unity, depending on whether the common part of the O+O systematic uncertainties cancels between centrality classes. This ordering is expected if Ne+Ne collisions have a larger transverse area at the same multiplicity and a larger area gives a softer spectrum. The softening decreases towards peripheral collisions and is the same at forward pseudorapidity. In central collisions the spectral shape follows the centrality class more closely than the multiplicity. The same procedure is tested in Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions.

papers.title: Branch and Consolidate: A Unified Recipe for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Specialists post-trained from a shared checkpoint acquire complementary capabilities, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) can consolidate them into a single model. However, we find that existing consolidation methods, from weight merging to MOPD, fall short when specialists diverge substantially from the shared checkpoint, whereas prior studies mostly examine specialists that remain close to it. We present a unified recipe for multimodal MOPD that consolidates such specialists back into the single student they branched from. The recipe specifies initialization, data selection, balanced supervision across teachers, and preservation of existing capabilities for consolidation, together with a targeted refinement stage for capabilities that still lag behind their specialists. In an industrial setting with six specialists, the student closely approaches each specialist in its own domain and surpasses the perception specialist. It recovers 97.0% of their average gain, compared with 79.8% for IM-MOPD. In the fully open five-domain setting with Qwen3-4B, our method recovers 95.7% of the specialists' average gain after consolidation and 97.5% after refinement, compared with 94.1% for IM-MOPD. We further analyze the full pipeline through mechanism ablations and training dynamics, providing practical guidance for diagnosing incomplete consolidation. Code will be released.

papers.title: Quantum Capacity with Incoherent Codes
papers.abstract: Arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise drives the quantum capacity to zero in every input basis when the encoder is restricted to incoherent operations. Even one qubit cannot then be sent reliably: if the output is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability $\varepsilon\le1/2$, the entanglement fidelity is at most $1-\varepsilon/2$ at every block length. With unrestricted decoding, a single-letter formula gives the capacity with incoherent encoding as the maximum Holevo information over ensembles of basis states with identical environment outputs. For either incoherent or unrestricted encoding, imposing incoherent decoding reduces the capacity by at most a factor of two; this factor is optimal. We bound the fidelity of incoherent decoders and evaluate the capacities with incoherent encoding for multiqubit Pauli channels.

papers.title: DiffAnchor: Anchor-Space Diffusion for Monocular 3D Hand Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient monocular 3D hand pose estimation is an important perception capability for embodied human interaction and dexterous manipulation. Recent diffusion-based methods model pose uncertainty by iteratively denoising 3D joint coordinates. However, directly diffusing the final joints requires the generative process to simultaneously explore plausible poses and recover precise coordinates, often relying on additional denoising steps or multiple hypotheses and consequently increasing inference cost. In this work, we propose DiffAnchor, a few-step anchor-space diffusion framework that diffuses anchors rather than joints. Our key insight is that stochastic exploration does not need to operate directly on the final output. Instead, diffusion searches for informative intermediate anchors that serve as local 3D regressors, while anchor-to-joint offset prediction and weighted aggregation complete precise joint localization. Specifically, fixed context anchors provide stable global references, whereas noisy dynamic anchors are iteratively refined toward informative joint regions. An importance-guided anchor selection and replenishment mechanism further retains useful anchors, removes ineffective ones, and explores insufficiently covered regions. This design reduces the precision burden of the diffusion process and enables accurate prediction using only a few denoising steps and a single hypothesis. Extensive experiments on HO-3D V2, NYU, ICVL, and InterHand2.6M demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on the first three benchmarks and competitive performance on challenging interacting-hand estimation, while maintaining inference efficiency comparable to deterministic regression baselines.

papers.title: Characterizing $2$-slices over finite groups
papers.abstract: For a finite group $G$, we characterize the $2$-slices of $G$-spectra in the regular slice filtration in terms of their homotopy Mackey functors and $k$-invariant. We explicitly compute this for cyclic $p$-groups and the alternating group $A_4$.

papers.title: Controlled teleportation of an unknown qutrit and its control power
papers.abstract: We propose a controlled quantum teleportation protocol for an arbitrary unknown qutrit using a nonmaximally entangled channel, with Charlie holding a qubit and Alice and Bob each holding a four-level particle. With the aid of an auxiliary qubit, the receiver can recover the input state probabilistically with unit fidelity. We derive the overall success probability and show that it is independent of the input state. To quantify the controller's authority, we obtain analytical expressions for the optimal average teleportation fidelities with and without the controller's cooperation, keeping the sender's joint measurement fixed and averaging uniformly over pure qutrit input states with all measurement outcomes included. Their difference defines the control power of the protocol. For the shared states considered here, we determine a controller measurement basis that simultaneously maximizes the control power and the teleportation success probability for a given shared state. These results clarify the role of the controller's measurement in controlled teleportation with unequal local dimensions.

papers.title: GeoVLDrive: Geometry-Grounded Vision-Language Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) planners inherit semantic knowledge from pretrained vision-language models, but their reasoning is rarely grounded in 3D scene structure and its evolution over time. We introduce GeoVLDrive, a geometry-grounded VLA framework for 3D spatiotemporal reasoning and planning. Multi-layer features from a 3D foundation model augment the vision-language backbone through gated cross-attention. A structured latent chain of thought (CoT) organizes future scene geometry, key-agent motion, and meta-actions into ordered, separately supervised latent states. An action expert generates trajectory proposals from these states and multi-layer scene features, and ranks them using scene-grounded, interacting score tokens. We also introduce NAVSIM 3DQA to train and evaluate metric 3D spatial and motion understanding. GeoVLDrive achieves 91.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2. On NAVSIM 3DQA, the geometry-grounded backbone scores 89.2% overall, 4.6 percentage points above the fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-2B baseline. On LingoQA, the backbone achieves 68.6% Lingo-Judge accuracy.

papers.title: Analysis of Federated Graph Neural Networks for Predicting Nuclear Core Properties
papers.abstract: Federated learning has grown in popularity owing to the increasing data privacy and safety concerns. It allows multiple parties to collaboratively train a model without exchanging their raw data. As an example of highly sensitive infrastructure of national importance, nuclear reactors benefit from this approach, where---while pooling multiple large datasets from different institutions could improve machine learning solutions---the confidentiality of the datasets is paramount. In this paper, we demonstrate that a graph neural network (GNN) outperforms the convolutional neural network (CNN) baseline in a federated setting for a use case concerning nuclear reactor core optimization. The GNN architecture is better suited for the nuclear reactor geometry as, unlike the CNN, it does not require padding the cylindrical core and does not assume translation invariance. The key finding of this work is that input representation is more important than model size and complexity. More sophisticated federated algorithms were employed, but the improvements derived were of lower magnitude. Experimenting with training corpus volume led to the discovery that greater fuel inventory variance is more beneficial than arrangements of existing cases, which is a direct consequence of data heterogeneity. Going forward, focus will remain on enhancing the input and readout representation.

papers.title: RecurSciBench: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement in Data-Driven Scientific Research
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are advancing the automation of data-driven scientific research. Recent advances in recursive self-improvement (RSI) offer the potential for these agents to continuously improve through experience, but evaluating transfer across scientific tasks requires executable, scientifically verifiable tasks and independent assessment of self-improvement gains. We introduce RecurSciBench, a scalable benchmark for evaluating RSI in data-driven scientific research. Its RecurSciPipe framework automatically constructs scientific modeling and data analysis tasks from raw datasets, with execution-based verification and scientific validity checks. RecurSciBench spans four scientific domains, multiple data modalities, and varied scientific objectives. We evaluate four RSI systems by comparing their initial and evolved states on independent tasks after evolution on source tasks, covering within-type, cross-type, and cross-domain transfer. Experiments show that the benefits of self-improvement vary across agent systems and scientific domains. Positive overall gains can coexist with regressions on individual tasks. Experience can transfer across task types and benefit other domains even without measurable gains in the source domain.

papers.title: Steiner porism and boundary value problems
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to describe several interpretations of Steiner chains of circles in terms of certain boundary value problems and give a short review of related results. Our approach and discussion are motivated by the recent results on the geometry of Steiner porism based on an apparently novel analytic parametrization of poristic circles obtained by A.Diakvnishvili and the present author. We also mention a few feasible problems and generalizations suggested by the constructions and considerations presented in the paper. Keywords: Steiner chain of circles, Steiner porism, curvature, invariant moments of curvatures, boundary value problem, Riemann-Hilbert problem, Brylinski loop space, circle packing

papers.title: Waveform Randomization for Secure ISAC Against Informed Eavesdroppers
papers.abstract: We study waveform-level protection of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) against a UAV-mounted eavesdropper (Eve) that knows the waveform construction and the phase-key generation rules. The novelty of this work is a systematic, budget-explicit attack analysis: instead of relying on undisclosed design details, we quantify what an informed Eve can learn and reconstruct, and how much computation this takes. We protect the sensing reference with Fourier-curve modulation, phase keys, and tangent Artificial Noise (AN), with burst- specific information shared over secure backhaul. We compare three key-generation rules against offline Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based sequence identification and online Adam and phase-aware expectation-maximization (EM) key recovery, under complete or partial nominal-sequence knowledge. A power- domain model couples residual key error with imperfect AN removal and predicts coherent delay locking. Results show that reusable key structure permits sequence identification even when demodulation fails, position-dependent keying raises recovery difficulty, and seed-expanded keying resists the evaluated clas- sifier within the learning budget. Waveform simulations under multipath, clutter, and echo accumulation confirm the sensing impact.

papers.title: An Integrated Remote Sensing and Machine Learning Framework for Mapping Hazard Associated with Leached Metals
papers.abstract: This study integrates satellite remote sensing, groundwater monitoring, and machine learning to map leached-metal-associated hazards at four coal combustion residual (CCR) sites in Virginia, USA. Constituent-specific groundwater concentrations were expressed as Hazard Quotients (HQ) and combined into a composite Hazard Index (HI). Predictors included Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, biophysical parameters, and spatiotemporal metrics (2019-2025), alongside soil, climate, hydrology, topography, and land cover. Six supervised classifiers were evaluated using spatially separated test blocks, feature-set ablation, and leave-one-site-out testing. Higher HQ coincided with lower vegetation indices in 24 of 33 metal-site combinations near monitoring wells (sign test p = 0.007). Well HI was negatively correlated with CIRE and canopy chlorophyll content at three sites (Spearman rho as low as -0.71). Random Forest achieved within-site HI classification accuracies of 0.768-0.924 and higher-HI-class recall of 0.965-0.999. For 34 constituent-site combinations, HQ classification accuracies ranged from 0.775 to 0.989. Environmental covariates generally contributed more predictive information than vegetation features. Removing vegetation predictors did not reduce performance, and distance to the CCR unit alone performed best at one site. Zero-shot cross-site accuracy declined to 0.734-0.749, no better than the majority-class baseline. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating satellite observations and environmental data with groundwater measurements for site-calibrated spatial hazard screening. The framework identifies indirect environmental associations rather than directly detecting dissolved metals, highlighting the importance of local calibration and independent validation.

papers.title: InducedTFMs: A Family of Sub-Quadratic Tabular Foundation Models Using Induced Attention
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) have emerged as a serious competitor to gradient-boosted trees, predicting on a new table in a single forward pass by in-context learning. However, their attention is quadratic in the number of samples and features, which caps pretraining at small synthetic tables and forces inference on large ones to rely on chunking or subsampling. Row-compression models reduce the feature-wise cost, but only by discarding the cell-level representation, and remain quadratic in the number of samples. We introduce InducedTFM, which replaces both attention stages of a bidimensional TFM with the induced attention of the Set Transformer, preserving cell-level representations while making its cost linear in both samples and features. Under a training budget matched to a full-attention TabICLv2 reimplementation, InducedTFM matches its accuracy on TabArena and on a benchmark of larger datasets, and clearly outperforms a kernel linear-attention baseline of the same asymptotic cost. It overtakes TabICLv2 in inference time on narrow tables, reaching a 30x speed-up at 640K rows, although row compression remains preferable on wide tables.

papers.title: Analyzing Single-Bit Flips on LLMs and Their Backbone-Matched VLMs
papers.abstract: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) enable offline weight analysis and are reused as backbones in vision-language models (VLMs), increasing the risk of bit-flip attacks that manipulate stored weight bits to induce malicious model behavior. An adversary could identify vulnerable bits on a public LLM and later flip the same locations in a deployed LLM or its backbone-matched VLMs. A single-bit flip is particularly practical in this setting because it is easier to achieve under hardware fault attacks than multi-bit flips. However, existing selectors are mostly limited to multi-bit flips, without in-depth analysis of single-bit flips. In this paper, we adapt representative data-free and data-based bit selectors to identify candidate bits. We evaluate each bit independently on source LLMs and at the same logical coordinates in backbone-matched VLMs (without re-search), considering both performance degradation and prediction patterns across multiple inputs. Results show impact of single-bit flips varies across selectors on LLMs and their backbone-matched VLMs. A single-bit flip can make the model tend to produce a repeated output string across different inputs. Our robustness analysis reveals vulnerabilities in terms of performance and prediction patterns.

papers.title: MRCT: An Object-Centric Two-Layer Control Architecture for Heavy-Payload Multi-Robot Transportation
papers.abstract: Cooperative transportation of heavy payloads by heterogeneous mobile manipulators requires coordinated payload motion, force distribution, and compliant physical interaction. This paper presents MRCT, an object-centric two-layer control architecture for multi-robot transportation. At the object level, a model predictive controller (MPC) generates a coordinated contact-force reference for the payload. At the robot level, whole- body impedance control (WBIC) modules on individual robots realise the reference through a confidence-based blending of velocity-tracking and impedance torques. The blending mechanism emphasises tracking when the joint-velocity error is small and increases compliance when tracking degrades because of abrupt reference changes or physical disturbances. Simulation and hardware experiments with a heterogeneous team comprising a single-arm and a dual-arm mobile manipulator transporting a near-rated table payload demonstrate accurate object tracking, regulated contact forces, and stable payload orientation. Parameter sensitivity studies, obstacle-avoidance transportation, and step-load disturbance experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of MRCT for reliable cooperative transportation under the evaluated conditions

papers.title: Déjà-VAE: Training-Free Consistent Editing with Pseudo-Invertible Encoders and Latent Back-Projection
papers.abstract: Consistency is essential to generative workflows: repeated processing should preserve information beyond the changes explicitly requested. In latent diffusion models, this requires stability both when moving between latent and pixel spaces and when applying successive edits. Autoencoding errors and unintended changes from the editing model can accumulate across these operations, progressively altering image structure, texture, and color. We introduce Déjà-VAE, a framework that combines exact autoencoding consistency with calibrated editing stabilization, without training or fine-tuning. Its autoencoding component converts a pretrained variational autoencoder into a surjective pseudo-invertible neural network, with a fixed gain balancing deviations from the pretrained encoder and decoder. The modified decoder $D'$ is an explicit nonlinear right inverse of the encoder $E'$, satisfying $E'(D'(z))=z$ by construction. Consequently, $D'$ is a reflexive generalized inverse: latent round trips preserve their input, up to numerical precision, and repeated image reconstruction is idempotent. To suppress editing drift, adaptive wavelet back-projection finds the closest latent to the editor's output in $\ell_2$, subject to matching the previous latent on wavelet coefficients whose changes fall below calibrated thresholds. This correction is applied once per turn, with no additional network evaluations after calibration. Together, these components support workflows that remain in latent space or interleave generation with pixel-space operations and constraints. Tests across models and editing benchmarks show less drift than stock pipelines and dedicated consistency methods.

papers.title: CalibTrack: Exploring Learned Heteroscedastic Covariance for Robust Multi-Camera Pedestrian Tracking
papers.abstract: Analytical multi-view multi-object tracking (MV-MOT) systems rely on measurement covariance estimates to guide association, fusion, and state estimation. These covariance estimates are typically heuristic, requiring hand-tuning to the specific deployment scenario. We investigate how learned heteroscedastic measurement covariance affects calibration and robustness in analytical multi-camera tracking. To support this analysis, we introduce CalibTrack, a detector-side predictor that replaces uniform measurement covariance with per-detection covariance. We evaluate CalibTrack on the WildTrack and MultiviewX pedestrian tracking datasets with multiple analytical tracker cores, including an identity-informed GM-PHD, JIPDA, and pruned delta-GLMB filter. We additionally evaluate robustness by simulating adverse weather conditions with stable diffusion, Gaussian noise, camera browning, and camera dropout. CalibTrack improves average adverse tracking performance over confidence-scaled covariance, while producing better calibrated predictions, indicating the value of heteroscedastic covariance within analytical tracking. Comparisons with stronger heuristic covariance methods show that the benefits of learned covariance remain bounded by the quality of available observations and the downstream tracker choice. Together, these findings provide a principled exploration of learned covariance estimation and its potential for uncertainty-aware analytical tracking.

papers.title: Learning Inelastic Homogenization with Memory: Deep Material Networks and Discrete Adjoints
papers.abstract: Deep material networks (DMNs) provide mechanically structured surrogate models for computational homogenization. Traditionally, they are identified from elastic data and subsequently extrapolated to inelastic responses. This procedure leverages highly efficient linear solvers and provides robust extrapolation to different inelastic constitutive laws. However, selecting the appropriate linear elastic training data for a given inelastic constitutive behavior is non-trivial. In this work, we identify the DMNs directly from macroscopic stress-strain trajectories. Applying automatic differentiation to such problems with history entails a huge memory demand, excluding most practically relevant problems. To mitigate, we derive a path-consistent discrete adjoint that avoids propagating parameter-wise state sensitivities by treating equilibrium and internal variable evolution over the complete loading history as coupled constraints. For a short-fiber composite with an elastoplastic matrix, the adjoint approach reproduces the sensitivities obtained by direct differentiation and by an independent automatic-differentiation implementation, while it requires only one backward solve of the linearized state equations per time step and avoids the parameter-wise propagation of state sensitivities. Inelastic training also improves predictive accuracy: A rank-$5$ DMN trained on inelastic trajectories outperforms a deeper rank-$8$ DMN trained on elastic homogenization data for different loading paths. This advantage is retained under perturbations of the constituent inelastic material parameters. The resulting inelastic trained DMNs preserve the same formulation for online deployment and remain several orders of magnitude faster than the full-field homogenization solver.

papers.title: The infinite-dimensional extended Bloch representation
papers.abstract: In the extended Bloch representation (EBR) of quantum mechanics, the Born probabilities of a measurement with N outcomes are the relative volumes of N regions of a simplex-shaped abstract membrane, whose points represent the "hidden" measurement interactions. However, when N tends to infinity, the volumes vanish and the uniform membrane concentrates at the center of the unit ball. We show that this problem can be solved by renormalization: if the radius of the generalized Bloch ball grows like N, the distances of the measurement interactions from the facets of the simplex become independent exponential random variables. This is the only growth with a non-degenerate limit, and the limit membrane, which cannot live in the limit of the generalized Bloch space without privileging some of the outcomes, is the projective limit of the finite-dimensional membranes and, once renormalized, the only distribution compatible with the Born rule. For a pure point spectrum, the regions of the membrane become cones, the particle representing the state recedes to infinity, and the lines along which the membrane collapses become parallel. For a continuous spectrum, a further magnification yields a Poisson point process and the Born rule for probability densities. We also show that the uniform membrane is the only one compatible with the Born rule in finite dimension, and that the mechanism can be read, in every dimension, as a race between independent exponential clocks.

papers.title: When Randomness Hides Quantum Simulation Errors
papers.abstract: Trotter formulas approximate quantum dynamics by discrete steps, but errors in measured observables can be much smaller than worst-case estimates. We investigate how this suppression depends on the degree of randomness in the input states. We show that the mean absolute observable-error bound for state 2-designs can be exponentially smaller in qubit number than the tight bound for state 1-designs. To characterize this error transition from 1-design to 2-design, we use the excess frame potential to quantify the ensemble's second-moment distance. We quantify departures from these random-state statistics through the frame potential, a measure of pairwise state overlaps, and identify the accessible observables most sensitive to the resulting deviations in mean-square error. Extending the analysis to a Hamiltonian trajectory whose frame potential decays as $1/T$ before saturation, we also obtain a sufficient $p$th-order Trotter number $\mathcal O(T^{1+3/(4p)})$ for evolution time $T$. These findings connect input-state statistics to the visibility of Trotter errors, giving a theoretical guarantee and foundation for practical quantum simulation.

papers.title: Assessing Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.abstract: As the use of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes more widespread in cyber-physical systems, it becomes increasingly important to design RL agents that are able to adapt to changes in their environments in order to maintain safety and reliability. This paper addresses the question of whether different classes of RL algorithm are more robust against forgetting previously learned behaviours, a critical issue in continual learning, in non-stationary environments. We evaluate the robustness of representative examples of three important classes of RL algorithm in a non-stationary autonomous parking environment. These are Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which is a model-free on-policy algorithm, Soft-Actor-Critic (SAC), which is a model-free off-policy algorithm, and Drama, which is a model-based algorithm. The agents must learn to successfully park in four different scenarios, which are presented successively, with parking spaces oriented at varying angles. We find off-policy algorithms appear to be more robust compared to on-policy algorithms due to their use of replay, while model-based algorithms do not appear to offer any direct advantage over model-free algorithms. These experiments also highlight the additional challenges of finding robust abstractions of the environment, and oversensitivity to hyperparameters.

papers.title: On fluctuation properties of the cumulative current in gTASEP on open chains
papers.abstract: We present preliminary results of our numerical study of the fluctuation properties of the cumulative current, JT, in the generalized totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (gTASEP) on open chains with Liggett boundary conditions. GTASEP is the ordinary TASEP (a model of 1D- traffic on a single track, having many diverse applications), where an additional term controlling clustering of the particles is added. Extensive numerical simulations are performed to determine the dependence of the second scaled cumulant C2 of the time integrated current, JT, on the system size, L, in the long-time limit, allowing for comparison between open and periodic geometries. Preliminary results for C2 in the maximum current phase show agreement with theoretical predictions about the Kardar-Parizi-Zhang universality of the gTASEP on a segment.

papers.title: Integral Hodge/Tate conjecture of quotients via weak approximation
papers.abstract: For a finite group acting on a smooth projective separably rationally connected variety over an algebraically closed field, we prove that the rational quotient map induces a surjection from the coinvariants of its second Kato homology onto the second Kato homology of any smooth projective quotient model (with coefficients invertible in the ground field). The integral Hodge and Tate conjectures for one-cycles consequently descend to such quotient models. The proof uses weak approximation over function fields to retain the image of a smooth fiber in the total space.

papers.title: CoFiNav: VLM-Guided Coarse-to-Fine Semantic Navigation for Open-Ended Last-Mile UAV Delivery
papers.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) delivery is an important application of the low-altitude economy, enhancing the flexibility and accessibility of last-mile logistics. Existing UAV delivery methods generally rely on precise terminal coordinates, predefined terminal specifications, or task-specific localization procedures, limiting the scope and flexibility of delivery. As UAV logistics becomes more intelligent, open-ended semantic descriptions offer a new paradigm for specifying terminal destinations. However, conventional aerial navigation methods have limited ability to generalize to delivery scenarios that require open-vocabulary terminal navigation. To enable this broader delivery paradigm, we propose CoFiNav, a VLM-guided coarse-to-fine UAV semantic navigation framework that progressively grounds relation-defined terminal destinations through hierarchical semantic search and active 3D observation. Given a task description, a coarse prior map from OpenStreetMap (OSM), and accumulated observations, CoFiNav uses a vision-language model (VLM) to determine which unresolved entity or spatial relation should be verified next. A geometry-aware module converts the semantic observation request into feasible viewpoints using RGB images and LiDAR, while conventional motion planning handles safe execution. Experiments across multiple urban environments show that CoFiNav outperforms representative adapted baselines in success rate while requiring shorter flight paths and fewer observations.

papers.title: On the maximal operator of the hybrid Hermite-Laguerre-Jacobi semigroup
papers.abstract: We consider the heat-diffusion semigroup related to expansions with respect to an orthogonal system emerging by taking arbitrary finite tensor products of classical Hermite, Laguerre and Jacobi polynomials. Our main result is the weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for the associated maximal operator. This implies pointwise almost everywhere boundary convergence of the semigroup to initial values for all initial conditions that are integrable against the orthogonality measure.

papers.title: X-3DComposer: Feed-Forward 3D Scene Composition with Any Assets from Any Views
papers.abstract: Composing an editable 3D scene from images requires an asset for each object and a layout that places the assets. 3D generation and CAD retrieval now supply the assets, but layout still lacks a general solution: scene generation methods couple it with generation, and pose estimators handle one object at a time and need true-size CAD models, depth, or iterative refinement. We present X-3DComposer, a feed-forward model that predicts the layout separately from asset generation. Given one or more images of a scene, the object masks, and an asset for each object from any source, it jointly predicts the rotation, translation, and per-axis scale of all objects in a single forward pass of about one second. The key idea is to treat objects as views: renders of the assets are processed together with the scene images by a multi-view geometry model adapted from VGGT-$Ω$, and each object pose follows in closed form from the cameras predicted for its renders. Camera intrinsics, camera poses, and depth are optional inputs. When the meshes produced by five scene generation methods are kept fixed and only their layout is replaced, the layouts of X-3DComposer are more accurate than the native layouts of these methods. Compared with the stand-alone layout model SceneMaker, it reduces the scene-level Chamfer distance by 52% on IndoorMix, our test set from six indoor datasets, and by 28% on 3D-FUTURE.

papers.title: Bound-preserving Flux Limiters for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws on Two-Dimensional Adaptive Moving Meshes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a bound-preserving finite-volume method on adaptive moving meshes for two-dimensional hyperbolic conservation laws. The proposed method extends our previous one-dimensional framework [Y. Gu, G. Hu, and T. Tang, Adaptive mesh methods for hyperbolic conservation laws with bound-preserving flux limiters, arXiv:2602.12580] to two dimensions within the arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework. The mesh velocity is determined by solving a moving mesh equation, allowing the numerical solution to evolve directly between consecutive time levels. A key challenge in this extension is to ensure compatibility between the evolution of the mesh geometry and the update of the numerical solution, as geometric information is essential to the convex decomposition underlying the bound-preserving construction in two dimensions. Specifically, the high-order scheme is reformulated as a convex combination of high-order sub-cell schemes, each of which is blended with its first-order counterpart to enforce the bound-preserving property. The discrete geometric conservation law ensures the compatibility needed to maintain this convex decomposition on moving meshes. The resulting correction acts locally at individual cell interfaces and is equivalent to applying a bound-preserving flux limiter, making the approach applicable to general unstructured or irregular meshes. The associated bound-preserving CFL conditions are established for both scalar conservation laws and the nonlinear Euler equations of gas dynamics. Extensive two-dimensional numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: When Knowledge-Tracing Rankings Depend on Available History: A Source-Correction and Matched-Information Audit on ASSISTments 2009 and 2015
papers.abstract: Knowledge-tracing benchmarks often compare models that have different access to a learner's previous responses. We examine how data provenance, history length, and representation affect those comparisons. First, we compare a pinned ASSISTments 2009 sequence mirror against the corrected official release. Of 4,148 learners represented in both, 817 have different ordered skill-response sequences; the mirror also contains fewer labeled events. Second, we retain earlier learner-disjoint model evaluations on the 2009 and 2015 datasets, distinguishing exploratory results from a corrective 2015 replication. Finally, we evaluate a new, nonoverlapping sample of 4,000 ASSISTments 2015 learners using three models constrained to the same one-event or 20-event prior-response window. On 20,592 test responses from 582 learners, the 20-event Brier scores were 0.17667 for count-based logistic regression, 0.17389 for an order-aware logistic model, and 0.17514 for a GRU. The GRU-minus-order-aware difference was 0.00125 (95% learner-cluster bootstrap interval [0.00008, 0.00243]); at one prior event, the corresponding difference was 0.00212 [0.00120, 0.00301]. Earlier comparisons had favored the GRU against simpler history summaries. The newer analysis instead favors a logistic comparator that represents order using the same permitted event stream. These results concern predictive performance on particular historical cohorts and model settings. They neither isolate an architectural effect nor establish generalization to contemporary classrooms.

papers.title: Dynamic stochastic multi-attribute group decision-making based on fractional-order stochastic dominance criteria
papers.abstract: The stochastic dominance criterion has been widely employed in stochastic multi-attribute decision making as a robust tool for quantitatively comparing decision-makers' preferences over alternatives. Existing research predominantly relies on integer-order stochastic dominance criteria within static modeling frameworks. However, the integer-order scale is often too coarse, and real-world decision-making typically occurs in dynamic environments, for which static methods are inadequate. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel dynamic stochastic multi-attribute group decision making model based on fractional-order stochastic dominance criteria. In this model, we introduce the priority degree under fractional-order stochastic dominance, which not only encompasses the priority degree under integer-order stochastic dominance, but also is applicable to decision-makers whose utility functions are not concave everywhere. Consequently, the proposed model captures the dominance relations between alternatives with greater accuracy and flexibility. Moreover, the model allows for the addition or removal of attributes and alternatives across decision periods, thereby exhibiting the applicability to any dynamic decision process. Numerical examples and comparative analyses show the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach, highlighting its broader applicability compared with conventional methods. This study enriches the theoretical foundation of dynamic stochastic multi-attribute group decision making and contributes to improving the reliability and precision of decision outcomes.

papers.title: Toward Extreme-Scale Full-Wave Maxwell Simulation: Low-Dispersion Discretization and a Massively Parallel Three-Grid Solver
papers.abstract: Full-wave simulation of three-dimensional time-harmonic Maxwell problems over hundreds of wavelengths leads to indefinite systems with tens to hundreds of billions of unknowns. We present a matrix-free three-grid solver for such systems and its implementation on GPUs and CPUs. The solver is built on an interpolated optimized finite-difference (IOFD) discretization on the Yee grid, whose compact face and edge filters keep the phase error small at 6 points per wavelength, and it applies the same compact stencil on all three grids: an unshifted intermediate-grid correction is preconditioned by a complex-shifted auxiliary cycle, so that one preconditioner application performs a fixed number of stencil sweeps and reductions with storage linear in the number of unknowns. The implementation uses a partition nested across the grids, $s$-step smoothers that need one global reduction per smoothing call, and bfloat16 storage of the smoother bases. On 216 GPUs, complete solves with approximately $71.7$ billion complex unknowns take 77--504 seconds in homogeneous and heterogeneous media, with weak-scaling efficiencies of 89--91\% per preconditioner application; strong scaling reduces solves with 2.7 billion unknowns to 4.5--18 seconds on 64 GPUs. A CPU implementation reaches approximately $574$ billion unknowns on 13\,824 cores, and the computed fields agree with the outgoing Green field over domains of up to 956 wavelengths per direction.

papers.title: The socle of the last term in a minimal injective resolution II
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a Gorenstein ring with left and right self-injective dimensions $n$. We prove that the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $_RR$ has an essential socle. It answers an open question of Iwanaga and Sato. As a consequence, we get that for any left $R$-module $M$ with injective dimension $n$, the last term of a minimal injective resolution of $M$ also has an essential socle.

papers.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
papers.abstract: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.

papers.title: Quantum Switches Under Congestion: Stabilization, Scheduling, and Performance
papers.abstract: Quantum Communications (QC) are set to revolutionize communications by employing and exploiting the properties of quantum systems. In this work, we analyse Quantum Switch Networks (QSN) comprised of quantum switches, both memory-equipped and all-optical switch types, to study the time evolution of the requests' queue lengths and how they behave under certain regimes given by various configurations of the network, all governed by the throughput-optimal, classical MaxWeight Scheduling Policy. The goals of this work are twofold: first, we study the queue length dynamics, evolution and equilibrium under the Fluid Queues Approximation model and as a discrete evolution problem, with the addition of a simple discarding policy that stabilizes any scheduling policy by the introduction of a friction-like term named \textit{discard term} inside the evolution equations. The second goal is the validation of the mechanism by comparing the discrete queue evolution of all-optical and memory-equipped quantum networks under different constraints and complex topologies like BCube and Fat-Tree, which are key topologies present on future Quantum Data Centres.

papers.title: CodeWAM: A Code World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Driving world models anticipate action consequences through representations of how the world evolves. For autonomous driving, these representations must capture both the surrounding scene and the ego vehicle's motion under a candidate plan. We propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that incorporates executable code as part of its world representation. Code represents ego dynamics by expressing how the vehicle state evolves under plan execution, while a learned visual model captures scene-dependent consequences. Executing the code produces a candidate-conditioned motion sequence, which is evaluated relative to the prior plan and recorded motion history. The resulting execution consequences and learned scene outcomes jointly represent the candidate's future, enabling the planner to assess both what a plan may lead to and how the vehicle transitions into that future. The selected plan becomes part of the next decision's execution context, linking successive choices within the model. CodeWAM achieves 93.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, 92.1 EPDMS on v2 navtest, and 50.6 EPDMS on NAVHARD. Further experiments demonstrate improved pairwise execution consistency and gains on Hydra-MDP and DrivoR without additional training, supporting executable code as a complementary representation for driving world models.

papers.title: COHERE4D: Training-Free Dense Surface Alignment for Coherent Metric 4D Human-Scene Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Human and scene foundation models offer complementary strengths for monocular 4D reconstruction: human models recover metric-scale body meshes but lack scene grounding, whereas scene models estimate globally consistent 3D geometry and camera motion without reliable metric scale. Crucially, both models reconstruct the same foreground human surface. Yet existing methods do not directly exploit this shared surface: lacking reliable foreground human geometry in scene reconstructions, earlier approaches either resort to sparse contact constraints or learn data-driven alignment modules that generalize poorly to out-of-distribution scenes. We present COHERE4D, a training-free framework that directly registers the human surfaces predicted by independently pretrained human and scene foundation models to reconstruct a coherent, metric 4D world. COHERE4D establishes dense, pixel-aligned 3D correspondences over the visible human surface and employs RANSAC with cross-frame consensus to suppress outliers from occlusion, background contamination, and depth noise. This formulation solves for two complementary geometric quantities: a sequence-level shared scale that calibrates scene geometry and camera motion to metric human size, and per-frame human translations that align camera-space human meshes with the scaled scene geometry to enforce spatial and temporal consistency. Across diverse backbones and benchmarks, COHERE4D substantially outperforms prior methods in human--scene alignment, metric scene and camera pose reconstruction, and global human motion estimation, adding only 4,ms/frame, enabling overall inference at up to 14 FPS.

papers.title: On the effective atmospheric-scale $Δm^2$ in neutrino oscillation
papers.abstract: We discuss an effective two-frequency description of the three-generation neutrino oscillation with the key quantity $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$, which unifies the effects of atmospheric-scale $Δm^2_{31}$-$Δm^2_{32}$ driven oscillations. As a solution to the minimization problem in vacuum, Nunokawa {\it et al.} obtained $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} } = Δm^2_{31} - (2E / L) \arctan \left\{ r_{2} \sin 2Δ_{21} / ( r_{1} + r_{2} \cos 2Δ_{21} ) \right\}$, where $Δ_{21} \equiv Δm^2_{21} L / (4 E)$ and $r_{i}$ are the mixing-angle dependent constants. Despite the skepticism for the $L/E$ dependence in this formula, we show, in fact, that this is an exact expression, which renders the probability formula also exact. We offer an appealing-to-intuition physical explanation for the $L/E$ dependence that it originates from the nature-designed three generation neutrinos. The way it is buried into $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$ is through the solar-effect renormalization to this quantity. With the physical interpretation of $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$ at hand, we aim at resolving the existing controversies on $Δm^2_{ \text{effective} }$ in this paper.

papers.title: VISE: Verifier-Independent Skill Self-Evolution with Feedback from Tool Implementations
papers.abstract: Agent skills provide reusable workflows that guide LLM agents in using tools. Refining these workflows requires feedback on missing or incorrect instructions, but task-specific verifiers are not always available. We propose VISE (Verifier-Independent Skill Evolution), a scripts-first approach that uses tool implementations to guide skill revision. It extracts tool capabilities, input requirements, usage conditions, and output formats from source code. Using the task request and execution trace, it compares this information with current workflow instructions to identify missing or conflicting steps. It then recommends specific edits to SKILL.md, linking each change to the relevant implementation and usage conditions. We evaluate VISE as an additional revision stage for four evolution methods on SkillsBench and SkillLearnBench. Compared with the corresponding No-verifier conditions, it improves overall average task success by 9.14-13.35 percentage points. The proportion of tasks solved in all three runs increases by 12.36-18.29 points. A case study shows how revised instructions connect tool outputs to later steps. These results support tool implementations as a practical feedback source for skill self-evolution.

papers.title: An adaptive finite element method for the interior problem of Helmholtz equations with generalized transmission boundary conditions
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new adaptive finite element method for solving the interior transmission problem with generalized transmission boundary conditions (GTBCs) involving a surface Laplace-Beltrami operator. A $\mathbb{T}$-coercivity technique relying on a lifting operator is established to show the well-posedness of the variational problem in appropriate nonstandard Sobolev spaces. Then both the a priori error estimates and a posteriori error estimates including the upper bound and local lower bound of the finite element discretization are constructed. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the accuracy and convergence of the adaptive finite element method. Extension and high efficiency of the proposed method for the computation of the interior transmission eigenvalues for the problem with GTBCs are also discussed numerically.

papers.title: Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $Λ$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems.
